PONYTAIL MODE ACTIVE — level: full

# Ponytail

You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. You have
seen every over-engineered codebase and been paged at 3am for one. The best
code is the code never written.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No drift back to over-building. Still active if
unsure. Off only: "stop ponytail" / "normal mode". Default: **full**.
Switch: `/ponytail lite|full|ultra`.

## The ladder

Stop at the first rung that holds:

1. **Does this need to exist at all?** Speculative need = skip it, say so in one line. (YAGNI)
2. **Stdlib does it?** Use it.
3. **Native platform feature covers it?** `<input type="date">` over a picker lib, CSS over JS, DB constraint over app code.
4. **Already-installed dependency solves it?** Use it. Never add a new one for what a few lines can do.
5. **Can it be one line?** One line.
6. **Only then:** the minimum code that works.

The ladder is a reflex, not a research project. Two rungs work → take the
higher one and move on. The first lazy solution that works is the right one.

## Rules

- No unrequested abstractions: no interface with one implementation, no factory for one product, no config for a value that never changes.
- No boilerplate, no scaffolding "for later", later can scaffold for itself.
- Deletion over addition. Boring over clever, clever is what someone decodes at 3am.
- Fewest files possible. Shortest working diff wins.
- Complex request? Ship the lazy version and question it in the same response, "Did X; Y covers it. Need full X? Say so." Never stall on an answer you can default.
- Two stdlib options, same size? Take the one that's correct on edge cases. Lazy means writing less code, not picking the flimsier algorithm.
- Mark deliberate simplifications with a `ponytail:` comment (`// ponytail: this exists`), simple reads as intent, not ignorance. Shortcut with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic)? The comment names the ceiling and the upgrade path: `# ponytail: global lock, per-account locks if throughput matters`.

## Output

Code first. Then at most three short lines: what was skipped, when to add it.
No essays, no feature tours, no design notes. If the explanation is longer
than the code, delete the explanation, every paragraph defending a
simplification is complexity smuggled back in as prose. Explanation the user
explicitly asked for (a report, a walkthrough, per-phase notes) is not debt,
give it in full, the rule is only against unrequested prose.

Pattern: `[code] → skipped: [X], add when [Y].`

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | The ladder enforced. Stdlib and native first. Shortest diff, shortest explanation. Default. |

Example: "Add a cache for these API responses."
- full: "`@lru_cache(maxsize=1000)` on the fetch function. Skipped custom cache class, add when lru_cache measurably falls short."

## When NOT to be lazy

Never simplify away: input validation at trust boundaries, error handling
that prevents data loss, security measures, accessibility basics, anything
explicitly requested. User insists on the full version → build it, no
re-arguing.

Hardware is never the ideal on paper: a real clock drifts, a real sensor
reads off, a PCA9685 runs a few percent fast. Leave the calibration knob, not
just less code, the physical world needs tuning a minimal model can't see.

Lazy code without its check is unfinished. Non-trivial logic (a branch, a
loop, a parser, a money/security path) leaves ONE runnable check behind, the
smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks: an `assert`-based
`demo()`/`__main__` self-check or one small `test_*.py`. No frameworks, no
fixtures, no per-function suites unless asked. Trivial one-liners need no
test, YAGNI applies to tests too.

## Boundaries

Ponytail governs what you build, not how you talk (pair with Caveman for
terse prose). "stop ponytail" / "normal mode": revert. Level persists until
changed or session end.

The shortest path to done is the right path.

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\Anton L\.claude\skills\design # Design The front door for all design work. Read this before writing a line of UI. **The rule this skill exists to enforce:** > **Brand derives direction. Skills supply craft. Themes are the last resort.** Every previous failure in this codebase came from inverting that: a specialist skill set the direction and the brand got repainted in the skill author's palette. Direction comes from the subject's own evidence. Skills contribute spacing, states, motion, and mechanics *inside* that direction. This file dispatches. It does not teach — the references carry the full detail and are the source of truth. Load the ones your branch names; never load a catalogue to make one pick. Over-eager loading is the largest avoidable cost of running this skill. --- ## Disciplines that hold across every branch Not branch-specific. They apply to new work, audit, redesign, study, and component-scope alike. **Read [`chain-discipline.md`](references/chain-discipline.md) first — it is resident, not routed.** It is the one file in this shelf that is about the chain rather than the page: nine rules won from a five-day run that spent 37 build rounds on 10 orders and still missed the level. Every rule in it came from a measurement, a review or a plan that lied to this chain and was believed. They govern how you measure (M1–M3), how you verify (V1–V2), how you orchestrate (O1–O2) and how you review (R1–R2), and the round ladder in § 5 is why the spiral happened. No builder, reviewer or orchestrator runs without it. 1. **Pre-emit self-critique.** Before handing back any output, score it 1–5 on six axes — Philosophy, Hierarchy, Execution, Specificity, Restraint, Variety. Anything **< 3** triggers a revision pass. Stamp the six scores at the top of the artifact (`/* design · pre-emit critique: P5 H4 E5 S4 R5 V5 */`). See [`slop-test.md`](references/slop-test.md) § Pre-emit self-critique. 2. **Honest copy — no fabricated content.** If the user did not supply a metric, do not invent one. Stat-led layouts, comparison rows, and proof bars must use real numbers, a placeholder (`—` plus a labelled grey block, "metric to confirm"), or a different macrostructure. *"+47 % conversion"*, *"trusted by 50,000+ teams"*, and *"10× faster"* are slop the moment they're invented. Same rule for testimonials, logos, and case-study counts. See [`anti-patterns.md`](references/anti-patterns.md) § Invented metrics and gate **46**. 3. **Locked tokens — no mid-render improvisation.** Once the direction is settled, every colour and every `font-family` declaration must reference a named token (`var(--color-accent)`, `font-family: var(--font-display)`). Inline OKLCH / hex / `rgb()` values, or a `font-family: "Some Font"` that bypasses the token block, are not allowed. If a value is needed that doesn't exist as a token, lift it into the token block as a new named variable, then reference it. See [`anti-patterns.md`](references/anti-patterns.md) § Mid-render token improvisation and gate **48**. 4. **Re-drawn chrome forbidden.** Never hand-build fake browser bars (URL pill + traffic-light dots), fake phone frames, fake code-block windows (mock title bar + dots wrapping a `
`), or fake IDE chrome — the user's environment already supplies real chrome. Use real screenshots wrapped in a `

# Design-audit · Alunix V3g R9 mot showcase-golvet

Underlag:
- Byggd sida: `tests/alunix-r8/runs/V3g/index.html` (R9 plus rättningarna nedan).
- Golvet: `skills/design/references/scroll/showcase-floor.md` § 2.
- Jämförelse: `journeys/era-residence.md` (rank 1).
- Tre granskare: heuristik, kritiker och a11y.

Allt nedan är mätt headless (1440×900, 768×1024, 390×844, 320×640) och läst som bild av mig.

## 1. Domen

R9-planen är byggd och verifierad i pixlar. Efter granskarnas rättningar finns inga kända fel

def blocking() -> bool:
    return os.environ.get("DESIGN_GATE_BLOCKING", "").strip() not in ("", "0", "false")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reference floor — the r6 failure this closes: builders loaded Skill(design)
# and wrote real UI without ever reading TASTE.md, a catalogue example, or
# (when the brief was scroll-choreographed) the scroll references. Loading
# the skill is not the same as having actually looked at anything it points
# to. This runs only in the UNLOCKED (no DESIGN.md) branch of main() — a
# locked project's contract enforcement above is unrelated and unaffected.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _motion_floor(cat_root: Path, slug: str) -> int:
    """motion_floor from entries/<slug>/entry.md frontmatter, -1 when absent."""
    try:
        head = (cat_root / "entries" / slug / "entry.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")[:3000]
    except Exception:
        return -1
    m = re.search(r"^motion_floor:\s*(\d)", head, re.M)
    return int(m.group(1)) if m else -1


def _check_reference_floor(root: Path) -> None:
    if os.environ.get("DESIGN_REF_FLOOR", "").strip().lower() == "off":
        return
    if L.disabled():
        return
    if not L.armed(root):
        return

    rows = L.scope_to_session(L.all_rows(root))
    ref_reads = [r for r in rows if r.get("event") == "ref-read"]

    cat_roots = L.catalogue_roots(root)
    cat_root = cat_roots[0] if cat_roots else (root / "design-catalogue")
    skill_roots = L.design_skill_roots()
    skill_root = skill_roots[0] if skill_roots else (L.HOME / ".agents" / "skills" / "design")

    missing = []

    # Loading the skill is the floor's first rung: the r7 probe (2026-09-06)
    # read every reference and still never invoked Skill(design), so the
    # procedure (Steps 0-6) was never in context. A skill-read of the
    # skill's own SKILL.md counts the same as the Skill tool.
    skill_loaded = any(
        (r.get("event") == "skill" and str(r.get("skill", "")).split()[0] == "design")
        or (r.get("event") == "skill-read" and r.get("skill") == "design"
            and Path(r.get("file", "")).name == "SKILL.md")
        for r in rows
    )
    if not skill_loaded:
        missing.append("Du har inte laddat Skill(design) — kedjans procedur (Steps 0–6) krävs innan första UI-filen.")

    if not any(r.get("cat") == "taste" for r in ref_reads):
        taste_path = (cat_root / "TASTE.md").as_posix()
        missing.append(f"Du har inte läst {taste_path} — smakreferensen krävs innan första UI-filen.")

    feedback_path_p = cat_root / "FEEDBACK.md"
    if feedback_path_p.exists() and not any(r.get("cat") == "feedback" for r in ref_reads):
        missing.append(f"Du har inte läst {feedback_path_p.as_posix()} — återkopplingen krävs innan första UI-filen.")

    # Catalogue evidence (T3, 2026-09-08). The old rule accepted ANY file
    # under entries/<slug>/ — one fold.webp cleared a floor whose prose asks
    # for 2-4 entries read as pixels and as text. r7 (2026-09-06/07) passed
    # that bar and still never ran Skill(design-catalog): the selection was
    # the orchestrator's memory, not the catalogue. Three rungs now:
    #   1. a catalogue-select row, written by scripts/catalogue/select.py,
    #      naming >= 2 slugs -- mechanical proof the choice came out of the
    #      whole catalogue rather than recall;
    #   2. per selected slug: entry.md AND its fold read, plus the extract's
    #      DESIGN.md when one exists on disk (missing extracts are a known
    #      catalogue gap, not the builder's fault);
    #   3. the fingerprint registry on a scroll brief (below).
    entries_path = (cat_root / "entries").as_posix()
    cat_reads = [r for r in ref_reads if r.get("cat") == "catalogue"]
    select_rows = [r for r in rows if r.get("event") == "catalogue-select"]
    # The LATEST selection is the lock. r8 R1 (2026-09-10): the V3c builder ran
    # select.py once against the unfilled skeleton (zero scores, alphabetical
    # top four) and once against the real draft; a union of both rows would
    # have denied R2 for four slugs that were never the lock. Re-running
    # select.py supersedes, it does not accumulate.
    selected: list[str] = []
    if select_rows:
        for slug in (select_rows[-1].get("slugs") or []):
            if slug and slug not in selected:
                selected.append(slug)

    if not select_rows:
        missing.append(
            "Ingen katalogvalsrad i sessionen — kör "
            "`python scripts/catalogue/select.py --brief <fil> --k 4` "
            "(eller Skill(design-catalog)) så att urvalet görs ur hela katalogen, "
            "inte ur minnet.")
    elif len(selected) < 2:
        missing.append(
            f"Katalogvalet gav {len(selected)} post — kedjan kräver minst två "
            f"(SKILL.md Step 1b: läs 2–4 poster). Kör select.py med --k 2 eller mer.")
    else:
        by_slug: dict[str, set] = {}
        for r in cat_reads:
            by_slug.setdefault(r.get("slug", ""), set()).add(r.get("kind", "other"))
        for slug in selected:
            kinds = by_slug.get(slug, set())
            want = []
            if "entry-md" not in kinds:
                want.append(f"{entries_path}/{slug}/entry.md")
            if "fold" not in kinds and "slice" not in kinds and "shot" not in kinds:
                want.append(f"{entries_path}/{slug}/fold.webp (som bild, inte som text)")
            if "design-md" not in kinds:
                try:
                    ex = cat_root / "entries" / slug / "extract"
                    if ex.is_dir() and any(ex.glob("*-design-language.md")):
                        want.append(f"{entries_path}/{slug}/extract/*-design-language.md")
                except Exception:
                    pass
            if want:
                missing.append(
                    f"Vald katalogpost `{slug}` är inte läst färdigt — saknas: "
                    + ", ".join(want))

    if not cat_reads:
        missing.append(f"Du har inte läst någon post under {entries_path} — minst ett katalogexempel krävs innan första UI-filen.")

    has_lock = any(
        r.get("cat") == "references" and Path(r.get("file", "")).name == "reference-lock.md"
        for r in ref_reads
    )
    if not has_lock:
        lock_path = (skill_root / "references" / "reference-lock.md").as_posix()
        missing.append(f"Du har inte läst {lock_path} — referenslåset krävs innan första UI-filen.")

    intent_rows = [r for r in rows if r.get("event") == "intent"]
    latest_scroll = bool(intent_rows) and intent_rows[-1].get("scroll") == 1
    route_scroll = any(
        r.get("event") == "route" and r.get("skill") == "design" and r.get("signal") == "scroll"
        for r in rows
    )
    if latest_scroll or route_scroll:
        scroll_basenames = {
            Path(r.get("file", "")).name for r in ref_reads if r.get("sub") == "scroll"
        }
        for fname in ("devices.md", "feel-and-fingerprint.md"):
            if fname not in scroll_basenames:
                p = (skill_root / "references" / "scroll" / fname).as_posix()
                missing.append(f"Du har inte läst {p} — scrollkoreografins referens krävs innan första UI-filen.")
        # The fingerprint gate is >= 4-of-6 against EVERY row of the registry.
        # A concept cannot clear a gate whose rows were never read, and the
        # registry is the only place earlier builds are written down.
        if not any(r.get("cat") == "registry" for r in ref_reads):
            missing.append(
                "Du har inte läst fingerprint-registret "
                "(wiki/projects/_index/design-fingerprints.md) — fingerprint-gaten "
                "(≥ 4/6 mot varje rad) kan inte hållas mot rader du inte sett.")
        # The showcase floor (Anton 2026-10-03: the chain must CALL the GSAP/Lenis
        # mechanisms, not only list them). showcase-floor.md § 1 asks for two
        # motion_floor-2 sheets read as pixels and the Era journey before the first
        # line of motion code; the GSAP/Lenis skills hold the API the page is built in.
        for fname in ("showcase-floor.md", "era-residence.md"):
            if fname not in scroll_basenames:
                sub = "journeys/" if fname == "era-residence.md" else ""
                p = (skill_root / "references" / "scroll" / f"{sub}{fname}").as_posix()
                missing.append(f"Du har inte läst {p} — showcase-golvet krävs innan första UI-filen.")
        sheets = {r.get("slug") for r in cat_reads if r.get("kind") == "motion-sheet"}
        floor2 = sorted(s for s in sheets if s and _motion_floor(cat_root, s) == 2)
        if len(floor2) < 2:
            missing.append(
                f"Du har läst {len(floor2)} rörelseark med motion_floor: 2 — golvet kräver två "
                f"({entries_path}/<slug>/motion/sheet.webp som bild; välj med "
                "`grep -l \"motion_floor: 2\" design-catalogue/entries/*/entry.md`). "
                "Namnge intro, övergångar och signaturobjekt du lånar i beslutsloggen.")
        loaded = {str(r.get("skill", "")).split()[0].split(":")[-1]
                  for r in rows if r.get("event") in ("skill", "skill-read")}
        for sk in ("lenis", "gsap-core", "gsap-scrolltrigger"):
            if sk not in loaded:
                missing.append(f"Du har inte laddat Skill({sk}) — rörelsemotorns API krävs innan första UI-filen (devices.md § Skills to load).")

    if not missing:
        return

    msg = "[design-gate · referensgolv]\n" + "\n".join(missing)
    L.deny(msg)


def _check_generation(event, root) -> None:
    """Two conditions before anything is queued at a paid backend.

    1. A `generation budget: N credits` line in a BRIEF.md under this root.
       r7 ran to a ceiling Anton set out loud and the log reconciles because of
       it; without a written ceiling there is nothing to reconcile against.
    2. A `get_cost` preflight earlier in the session. The cost is readable
       without queueing a job, so spending without reading it is a choice, not
       a constraint.

    Advisory by default, like the rest of this hook: it denies, and
    DESIGN_GEN_GATE=off turns it off for a session that knows what it is doing.
    """
    if os.environ.get("DESIGN_GEN_GATE", "").strip().lower() == "off":
        return
    rows = L.scope_to_session(L.all_rows(root))

    budget = None
    for brief in list(root.glob("**/BRIEF.md"))[:40]:
        try:
            m = re.search(r"generation budget:\s*([0-9]+(?:[.,][0-9]+)?)",
                          brief.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"), re.I)
        except Exception:
            continue
        if m:
            budget = m.group(1)
            break

    missing = []
    if budget is None:
        missing.append("Ingen `generation budget: N credits`-rad i nagon BRIEF.md under "
                       "projektet. Skriv taket innan du koar ett betalt jobb "
                       "(references/generation.md § Kreditgrinden).")
    if not any(r.get("event") == "generation" and r.get("preflight") for r in rows):
        missing.append("Ingen `get_cost`-preflight i sessionen. Kor samma anrop med "
                       "`get_cost: true` forst och las kostnaden.")
    if missing:
        L.deny("[design-gate · genereringsgrind]\n" + "\n".join(missing))

        return

            _check_generation(event, L.project_root({"cwd": event.get("cwd")}))
        return

    # 2026-09-09: `cat > B.html <<'EOF'` sailed past the reference floor and
    # left no ledger row). Deny it in an armed session and point at Write/Edit,
    # where the floor and the contract can actually read the content.
    if L.tool_name(event) in SHELL_TOOLS:
        cmd = str(L.tool_input(event).get("command") or "")
        targets = L.shell_ui_write_targets(cmd)
        if not targets:
            return
        root = L.project_root({"cwd": event.get("cwd")})
        msg = ("[design-gate · skalskrivning]\n"
               "UI-filer författas bara med Write eller Edit, så att referensgolvet och "
               "kontraktet kan granska innehållet. Skalvägen kringgår båda: "
               + ", ".join(targets) +
               "\nKopiera (cp, mv, Copy-Item) är tillåtet. Omdirigering, heredoc, tee, "
               "sed -i, Set-Content/Out-File och inline-skript som skriver filen är det inte.")
        if L.armed(root):
            L.log(root, event="gate-deny", file=targets[0],
                  component=L.component_of(targets[0]), signal="shell-write",
                  detail=cmd[:160], tier=L.tier(root))
            L.deny(msg)
        else:
            L.emit("PreToolUse", msg + "\n(Sessionen är inte armad, så detta är en varning, inte ett nej.)")
        return

    if L.tool_name(event) not in WRITE_TOOLS:

77	### 2b. Seen at 60 frames (`MOTION_FRAMES=60`, 2026-10-03)
78	
79	The 20-frame sheet hid how the acts hand over. At 60 frames each transition shows its material:
80	
81	- **The bowl hands its colour on.** The half-moon of act 2 carries "Three reasons to choose Era"
82	  along its curve; it rises in pale sky blue and, fully grown, *is* the benefits section's ground.
83	  The transition and the next act are the same colour field. Nothing fades; the shape becomes the
84	  ground.
85	- **Flowers bridge the ground change.** Where pale blue turns to cream (benefits → concept), a
86	  bougainvillea cut-out enters from the lower edge first and the cream follows it, so the change
87	  has a cause on screen before it happens.
88	- **Clouds carry the route into the master plan.** The hand-drawn route of the horizontal passage
89	  runs into a bank of clouds; the clouds part onto the aerial render. Act 5 → 6 is a camera
90	  descending through weather, not a cut.
91	- **The reverse grow.** After the master plan the full-bleed aerial shrinks back into a framed
92	  card on pale blue (the typology slider). The same card ↔ full-bleed move is used in both
93	  directions, which is what makes it read as one system.

95	  first screen comes back as rectangular colour panels holding bougainvillea photos, and the
96	  closing "ARCHITECTURE" sets condensed type across the photograph (rule 5: type and media in one
97	  frame).
98	
99	House reading: rule 2 of `showcase-floor.md` is met here by *one* material per transition (a
100	shape, a plant, weather, a card), each taken from the subject itself. That is the bar for the
101	Alunix next round (AUDIT-ALUNIX-R9.md § 4).
102	
103	## 3. What makes it a journey (the part to keep)
104	
105	1. **One shape is the thread.** The arch is the loader's exit, the mid-page bowl with text on
106	   its rim, the pair of windows in the architecture act, and the closing frame. The visitor
107	   never names it, but the page feels like one building.
108	2. **Camera, not sections.** The hero is a descent; the amenities leave by zooming past the
109	   lens; the location turns the page sideways; the end pulls back into a window. Acts are
110	   *moves of one camera*, and each transition has a material cause (rule 2 of the floor).
111	3. **Alternation.** Full-bleed photo → cream text chapter → photo → pale-blue chapter. Never two
112	   dark photo acts in a row, never two text chapters in a row. Rest beats (the quote) every
113	   third act.
114	4. **One passage of a different axis.** A single horizontal stretch in a vertical page, placed
115	   after the first third, carrying the biggest type on the site.
116	5. **A living material that crosses the chapters.** Bougainvillea video loops bleed in from
117	   the frame edges in five different acts, each time larger or from another side.
118	6. **Text behaves the same way everywhere.** Every heading arrives the same way (chars standing
119	   up), every paragraph the same way (masked lines), every script word the same way — and then
120	   it stands still. Consistency of reveal is what lets the big moves read as big.
121	7. **The ending answers the opening.** Door in, window out.
122	8. **Tempo is set, not left to the wheel.** Lenis 1.2 s duration, chapters that snap, a hero of
123	   five screens, scrub values of 0.25–0.5 — slow enough that nothing is missed (F-020).
124	
125	## 4. Rebuild recipe (house toolchain)
126	
127	Static HTML with the importmap from `toolchain.md`; `./gsap.js` exports `gsap, ScrollTrigger,
128	SplitText, CustomEase, Flip, DrawSVGPlugin`; `./smooth-scroll.js` exports the Lenis instance
129	with the house tempo (`lerp .075`, `wheelMultiplier .6`) — do not copy Era's Lenis numbers.
130	
131	```js
132	import { gsap, ScrollTrigger, SplitText, CustomEase, DrawSVGPlugin } from "./gsap.js";
133	import lenis from "./smooth-scroll.js";
134	
135	// tokens — rename per project, never reuse the values as a set
136	CustomEase.create("inOut", "0.75,0,0.25,1"); CustomEase.create("out", "0.25,1,0.5,1");
137	CustomEase.create("in", "0.5,0,0.75,0");     CustomEase.create("dive", "0.6,0,0,1");
138	const D = { s: 0.4, m: 0.8, l: 1.2, stagger: 0.1 };
139	
140	// 0→1  the door: a masked opening that rises, widens, and we pass through
141	const door = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });
142	door.to(":root", { "--door-w": "36vw", "--door-y": "15vh", duration: 1.5, ease: "inOut" })
143	    .to(":root", { "--door-w": "125vw", "--door-y": "-100vh", duration: 2.4, ease: "dive" })
144	    .fromTo(".hero-plate", { scale: 0.75 }, { scale: 1, duration: 3.9, ease: "dive" }, 0);
145	// overture copy reveals first (SplitText masks), a hold, then door.play()
146	
147	// 1  hero descent: ~5 screens, one camera move, heading still ≥ 40 vh
148	gsap.timeline({ scrollTrigger: { trigger: ".hero-area", start: "top top", end: "bottom bottom", scrub: 0.5 } })
149	  .to(".hero-copy", { yPercent: -40, ease: "none" }, 0)
150	  .to(".hero-plate", { yPercent: -15, ease: "none" }, 0)
151	  .to({}, { duration: 0.35 })                                            // the still beat
152	  .to(".hero-plate", { scale: 2, transformOrigin: "50% 75%", ease: "in" });
153	// .hero-area is 500vh tall; .hero-w is position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100vh
154	
155	// 2  the bowl: a shape rises and grows into the next ground, its rim carrying a sentence
156	gsap.timeline({ scrollTrigger: { trigger: ".bowl", start: "top bottom", end: "top top", scrub: 0.4 } })
157	  .fromTo(".bowl-shape", { yPercent: 60, scale: 0.8 }, { yPercent: 0, scale: 1.6, ease: "none" })
158	  .to(".bowl-rim-text", { attr: { "word-spacing": "10rem" } }, 0);     // <textPath> on the arc
159	
160	// 3  slide wipe (the recurring image transition)
161	const wipeIn = (img) => gsap.timeline()
162	  .fromTo(img.parentElement, { clipPath: "polygon(100% 0,100% 0,101% 100%,125% 100%)" },
163	          { clipPath: "polygon(0 0,100% 0,100% 100%,0 100%)", duration: D.l, ease: "inOut" })
164	  .fromTo(img, { scale: 1.5, xPercent: 25 }, { scale: 1, xPercent: 0, duration: D.l, ease: "inOut" }, 0);
165	
166	// 5  the sideways passage
167	const track = document.querySelector(".track");
168	const pan = gsap.to(track, { x: () => -(track.scrollWidth - innerWidth), ease: "none",
169	  scrollTrigger: { trigger: ".passage", pin: true, start: "top top", scrub: 0.25,
170	                   end: () => "+=" + (track.scrollWidth - innerWidth), invalidateOnRefresh: true } });
171	gsap.fromTo("#route", { drawSVG: "0%" }, { drawSVG: "100%", ease: "none",
172	  scrollTrigger: { containerAnimation: pan, trigger: "#route", start: "left 70%", end: "right 40%", scrub: 0.4 } });
173	
174	// 14  the window closes
175	gsap.timeline({ scrollTrigger: { trigger: ".outro", start: "top 30%", end: "bottom bottom", scrub: 0.5 } })
176	  .to(".outro-plate", { clipPath: "inset(8% 22% 8% 22%)", ease: "none" })
177	  .fromTo(".footer", { autoAlpha: 0, scale: 0.75 }, { autoAlpha: 1, scale: 1, ease: "none" }, 0);
178	
179	// text, the same way everywhere
180	document.fonts.ready.then(() => {
181	  SplitText.create("[data-reveal=p]", { type: "lines", mask: "lines", autoSplit: true,
182	    onSplit: s => gsap.from(s.lines, { yPercent: 110, duration: D.l, ease: "out", stagger: D.stagger,
183	      scrollTrigger: { trigger: s.elements[0], start: "top 85%", once: true } }) });
184	  SplitText.create("[data-reveal=h]", { type: "chars,words", autoSplit: true,
185	    onSplit: s => gsap.from(s.chars, { yPercent: 50, rotateY: 90, autoAlpha: 0, duration: D.m, ease: "out", stagger: 0.05,
186	      scrollTrigger: { trigger: s.elements[0], start: "top 85%", once: true } }) });
187	});
188	
189	// chapter snap through Lenis (never ScrollTrigger snap at page level)
190	let t; lenis.on("scroll", () => { clearTimeout(t); t = setTimeout(() => {
191	  const hit = [...document.querySelectorAll("[data-snap]")].find(s => { const r = s.getBoundingClientRect();
192	    return Math.min(r.bottom, innerHeight) - Math.max(r.top, 0) > innerHeight * 0.5 && r.top !== 0; });
193	  hit && lenis.scrollTo(hit, { duration: 1.2 }); }, 60); });
194	```
195	
196	Verification stays the house's: `section_probe.py` on the whole page against the baseline
197	(F-021), `motion_probe.py` for staircase/frame time (F-013), the contact sheet read by the lead,
198	and the two floor-2 references open beside it (`showcase-floor.md` § 1).
199	
200	## 5. Variation slots — how the next page is *not* Era
201	
202	Fill every slot differently from Era and from the last house page; the fingerprint gate
203	(`feel-and-fingerprint.md`) checks it, but decide it here first.
204	
205	| Slot | Era | Other answers seen in the catalogue |
206	|---|---|---|
207	| The thread shape | an arch (architecture) | a lens (elegantseagulls), a letter counter (khanhnguyen's parting word), a window in a photo (Hōrai), a vinyl (lesburgersdecolette), a cube unfolding (d2c-lifescience), a pen standing in the sentence (nota), a bolt that wipes (agencefoudre) |
208	| The door (overture → hero) | fly through the shape | counter → mark (ddark, nickho), copy first then light (seewhateyesee), curtain/push (filmbot), letters out of blur (millemann), object in the loader (ikea), pixel-block dissolve (davidecattaneo, meesverberne) |
209	| The camera | descent, then zoom past | dolly into a drawing (illoca), corridor of photos (thisisonward), orbit a product (neiru), a walk through rooms (maximeguillon), a room of text (stabondar) |
210	| The living material | flower video loops at the edges | smoke, grain, paper fibre, a drifting cloud marquee, cut-out people (vazzi), stickers, a ribbon (digidop) |
211	| The passage of a different axis | one horizontal location chapter | a vertical column wall (markclennon), a checkerboard swap (thomasmonavon), a tilted plane (wodniack), a 3D ring (annnimate) |
212	| The reveal grammar | chars standing up / masked lines | words lighting grey→ink (forge, filmbot), lines through blur (12 studio), scramble (modus), letters bobbing (flashform) |
213	| The rest beat | a quote over a parallax pool | a single full-bleed still, a line drawing, silence on a flat ground |
214	| The ending | the photo becomes a framed window | the shape returns as the sign-off (heart mask → staircase, maelruffini), the wordmark melts back (thisisbond), Hello/Bye bookends (huge), the loader object sprints across the lab (runrobrun) |
215	| Tempo | Lenis 1.2 s, snap, scrub .25–.5 | house tempo fixed; vary act length and the position of the peak instead |
216	
217	Rule of thumb: change the **shape, the material and the door** and the page is already its own;
218	keep the eight journey properties in § 3 and it will still feel like a trip.
219	
220	## 6. Below the floor on Era itself (not to copy)
221	
222	- `prefers-reduced-motion` is not read anywhere — consistent with the house (F-011), noted
223	  only because the a11y audit will ask.
224	- No `<img>` has `width`/`height`; srcset tops at 1920 w; `html { font-size: 1vw }` makes
225	  every rem scale with the viewport (type gets very small on narrow desktops).
226	- A Swiper init that never runs (dead code), and the location and architecture acts are
227	  desktop-only — mobile gets a flatter page. The house version keeps the acts on mobile as
228	  stacked scenes.
229	- First-visit-only overture via `sessionStorage`: fine, but the repeat-visit door must still
230	  satisfy rule 1 (something persists across the handoff) — on Era it does, the dive stays.

### 2b. Seen at 60 frames (`MOTION_FRAMES=60`, 2026-10-03)

The 20-frame sheet hid how the acts hand over. At 60 frames each transition shows its material:

- **The bowl hands its colour on.** The half-moon of act 2 carries "Three reasons to choose Era"
  along its curve; it rises in pale sky blue and, fully grown, *is* the benefits section's ground.
  The transition and the next act are the same colour field. Nothing fades; the shape becomes the
  ground.
- **Flowers bridge the ground change.** Where pale blue turns to cream (benefits → concept), a
  bougainvillea cut-out enters from the lower edge first and the cream follows it, so the change
  has a cause on screen before it happens.
- **Clouds carry the route into the master plan.** The hand-drawn route of the horizontal passage
  runs into a bank of clouds; the clouds part onto the aerial render. Act 5 → 6 is a camera
  descending through weather, not a cut.
- **The reverse grow.** After the master plan the full-bleed aerial shrinks back into a framed
  card on pale blue (the typology slider). The same card ↔ full-bleed move is used in both
  directions, which is what makes it read as one system.
- **The overture's burgundy returns as blocks.** In "The space to live in" the burgundy of the
  first screen comes back as rectangular colour panels holding bougainvillea photos, and the
  closing "ARCHITECTURE" sets condensed type across the photograph (rule 5: type and media in one
  frame).

House reading: rule 2 of `showcase-floor.md` is met here by *one* material per transition (a
shape, a plant, weather, a card), each taken from the subject itself. That is the bar for the
Alunix next round (AUDIT-ALUNIX-R9.md § 4).

## 3. What makes it a journey (the part to keep)

1. **One shape is the thread.** The arch is the loader's exit, the mid-page bowl with text on
   its rim, the pair of windows in the architecture act, and the closing frame. The visitor
   never names it, but the page feels like one building.
2. **Camera, not sections.** The hero is a descent; the amenities leave by zooming past the
   lens; the location turns the page sideways; the end pulls back into a window. Acts are
   *moves of one camera*, and each transition has a material cause (rule 2 of the floor).
3. **Alternation.** Full-bleed photo → cream text chapter → photo → pale-blue chapter. Never two
   dark photo acts in a row, never two text chapters in a row. Rest beats (the quote) every
   third act.
4. **One passage of a different axis.** A single horizontal stretch in a vertical page, placed
   after the first third, carrying the biggest type on the site.
5. **A living material that crosses the chapters.** Bougainvillea video loops bleed in from
   the frame edges in five different acts, each time larger or from another side.
6. **Text behaves the same way everywhere.** Every heading arrives the same way (chars standing
   up), every paragraph the same way (masked lines), every script word the same way — and then
   it stands still. Consistency of reveal is what lets the big moves read as big.
7. **The ending answers the opening.** Door in, window out.
8. **Tempo is set, not left to the wheel.** Lenis 1.2 s duration, chapters that snap, a hero of
   five screens, scrub values of 0.25–0.5 — slow enough that nothing is missed (F-020).

## 4. Rebuild recipe (house toolchain)

Static HTML with the importmap from `toolchain.md`; `./gsap.js` exports `gsap, ScrollTrigger,
SplitText, CustomEase, Flip, DrawSVGPlugin`; `./smooth-scroll.js` exports the Lenis instance
with the house tempo (`lerp .075`, `wheelMultiplier .6`) — do not copy Era's Lenis numbers.

```js
import { gsap, ScrollTrigger, SplitText, CustomEase, DrawSVGPlugin } from "./gsap.js";
import lenis from "./smooth-scroll.js";

// tokens — rename per project, never reuse the values as a set
CustomEase.create("inOut", "0.75,0,0.25,1"); CustomEase.create("out", "0.25,1,0.5,1");
CustomEase.create("in", "0.5,0,0.75,0");     CustomEase.create("dive", "0.6,0,0,1");
const D = { s: 0.4, m: 0.8, l: 1.2, stagger: 0.1 };

// 0→1  the door: a masked opening that rises, widens, and we pass through
const door = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });
door.to(":root", { "--door-w": "36vw", "--door-y": "15vh", duration: 1.5, ease: "inOut" })
    .to(":root", { "--door-w": "125vw", "--door-y": "-100vh", duration: 2.4, ease: "dive" })
    .fromTo(".hero-plate", { scale: 0.75 }, { scale: 1, duration: 3.9, ease: "dive" }, 0);
// overture copy reveals first (SplitText masks), a hold, then door.play()

// 1  hero descent: ~5 screens, one camera move, heading still ≥ 40 vh
gsap.timeline({ scrollTrigger: { trigger: ".hero-area", start: "top top", end: "bottom bottom", scrub: 0.5 } })
  .to(".hero-copy", { yPercent: -40, ease: "none" }, 0)
  .to(".hero-plate", { yPercent: -15, ease: "none" }, 0)
  .to({}, { duration: 0.35 })                                            // the still beat
  .to(".hero-plate", { scale: 2, transformOrigin: "50% 75%", ease: "in" });
// .hero-area is 500vh tall; .hero-w is position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100vh

// 2  the bowl: a shape rises and grows into the next ground, its rim carrying a sentence
gsap.timeline({ scrollTrigger: { trigger: ".bowl", start: "top bottom", end: "top top", scrub: 0.4 } })
  .fromTo(".bowl-shape", { yPercent: 60, scale: 0.8 }, { yPercent: 0, scale: 1.6, ease: "none" })
  .to(".bowl-rim-text", { attr: { "word-spacing": "10rem" } }, 0);     // <textPath> on the arc

// 3  slide wipe (the recurring image transition)
const wipeIn = (img) => gsap.timeline()
  .fromTo(img.parentElement, { clipPath: "polygon(100% 0,100% 0,101% 100%,125% 100%)" },
          { clipPath: "polygon(0 0,100% 0,100% 100%,0 100%)", duration: D.l, ease: "inOut" })
  .fromTo(img, { scale: 1.5, xPercent: 25 }, { scale: 1, xPercent: 0, duration: D.l, ease: "inOut" }, 0);

// 5  the sideways passage
const track = document.querySelector(".track");
const pan = gsap.to(track, { x: () => -(track.scrollWidth - innerWidth), ease: "none",
  scrollTrigger: { trigger: ".passage", pin: true, start: "top top", scrub: 0.25,
                   end: () => "+=" + (track.scrollWidth - innerWidth), invalidateOnRefresh: true } });
gsap.fromTo("#route", { drawSVG: "0%" }, { drawSVG: "100%", ease: "none",
  scrollTrigger: { containerAnimation: pan, trigger: "#route", start: "left 70%", end: "right 40%", scrub: 0.4 } });

// 14  the window closes
gsap.timeline({ scrollTrigger: { trigger: ".outro", start: "top 30%", end: "bottom bottom", scrub: 0.5 } })
  .to(".outro-plate", { clipPath: "inset(8% 22% 8% 22%)", ease: "none" })
  .fromTo(".footer", { autoAlpha: 0, scale: 0.75 }, { autoAlpha: 1, scale: 1, ease: "none" }, 0);

// text, the same way everywhere
document.fonts.ready.then(() => {
  SplitText.create("[data-reveal=p]", { type: "lines", mask: "lines", autoSplit: true,
    onSplit: s => gsap.from(s.lines, { yPercent: 110, duration: D.l, ease: "out", stagger: D.stagger,
      scrollTrigger: { trigger: s.elements[0], start: "top 85%", once: true } }) });
  SplitText.create("[data-reveal=h]", { type: "chars,words", autoSplit: true,
    onSplit: s => gsap.from(s.chars, { yPercent: 50, rotateY: 90, autoAlpha: 0, duration: D.m, ease: "out", stagger: 0.05,
      scrollTrigger: { trigger: s.elements[0], start: "top 85%", once: true } }) });
});

// chapter snap through Lenis (never ScrollTrigger snap at page level)
let t; lenis.on("scroll", () => { clearTimeout(t); t = setTimeout(() => {
  const hit = [...document.querySelectorAll("[data-snap]")].find(s => { const r = s.getBoundingClientRect();
    return Math.min(r.bottom, innerHeight) - Math.max(r.top, 0) > innerHeight * 0.5 && r.top !== 0; });
  hit && lenis.scrollTo(hit, { duration: 1.2 }); }, 60); });
```

Verification stays the house's: `section_probe.py` on the whole page against the baseline
(F-021), `motion_probe.py` for staircase/frame time (F-013), the contact sheet read by the lead,
and the two floor-2 references open beside it (`showcase-floor.md` § 1).

## 5. Variation slots — how the next page is *not* Era

Fill every slot differently from Era and from the last house page; the fingerprint gate
(`feel-and-fingerprint.md`) checks it, but decide it here first.

| Slot | Era | Other answers seen in the catalogue |
|---|---|---|
| The thread shape | an arch (architecture) | a lens (elegantseagulls), a letter counter (khanhnguyen's parting word), a window in a photo (Hōrai), a vinyl (lesburgersdecolette), a cube unfolding (d2c-lifescience), a pen standing in the sentence (nota), a bolt that wipes (agencefoudre) |
| The door (overture → hero) | fly through the shape | counter → mark (ddark, nickho), copy first then light (seewhateyesee), curtain/push (filmbot), letters out of blur (millemann), object in the loader (ikea), pixel-block dissolve (davidecattaneo, meesverberne) |
| The camera | descent, then zoom past | dolly into a drawing (illoca), corridor of photos (thisisonward), orbit a product (neiru), a walk through rooms (maximeguillon), a room of text (stabondar) |
| The living material | flower video loops at the edges | smoke, grain, paper fibre, a drifting cloud marquee, cut-out people (vazzi), stickers, a ribbon (digidop) |
| The passage of a different axis | one horizontal location chapter | a vertical column wall (markclennon), a checkerboard swap (thomasmonavon), a tilted plane (wodniack), a 3D ring (annnimate) |
| The reveal grammar | chars standing up / masked lines | words lighting grey→ink (forge, filmbot), lines through blur (12 studio), scramble (modus), letters bobbing (flashform) |
| The rest beat | a quote over a parallax pool | a single full-bleed still, a line drawing, silence on a flat ground |
| The ending | the photo becomes a framed window | the shape returns as the sign-off (heart mask → staircase, maelruffini), the wordmark melts back (thisisbond), Hello/Bye bookends (huge), the loader object sprints across the lab (runrobrun) |
| Tempo | Lenis 1.2 s, snap, scrub .25–.5 | house tempo fixed; vary act length and the position of the peak instead |

Rule of thumb: change the **shape, the material and the door** and the page is already its own;
keep the eight journey properties in § 3 and it will still feel like a trip.

## 6. Below the floor on Era itself (not to copy)

- `prefers-reduced-motion` is not read anywhere — consistent with the house (F-011), noted
  only because the a11y audit will ask.
- No `<img>` has `width`/`height`; srcset tops at 1920 w; `html { font-size: 1vw }` makes
  every rem scale with the viewport (type gets very small on narrow desktops).
- A Swiper init that never runs (dead code), and the location and architecture acts are
  desktop-only — mobile gets a flatter page. The house version keeps the acts on mobile as
  stacked scenes.
- First-visit-only overture via `sessionStorage`: fine, but the repeat-visit door must still
  satisfy rule 1 (something persists across the handoff) — on Era it does, the dive stays.

18	rules below are those five lies and their fixes, plus the four method changes

26	## 1 · Measurement
27	
28	### M1 · Register every custom property before you read it
29	
30	`getPropertyValue('--tx')` on an **unregistered** custom property returns the
31	token stream — `clamp(0,calc((0.3214 - 0.2258) / 0.1613),1)` — not a number.
32	`parseFloat` on that is `NaN`, and `NaN` silently compares as `0` in every filter
33	and every `if`.
34	
35	**What it cost:** the `--slit-p` filter was inert through round 18 *and* through
36	two of Astra's review passes without anyone noticing. It then convinced the lead
37	that a colour draw had not started when `--tx` was in fact `0.59`, and that
38	false reading was written up as a finding before it was caught.
39	
40	**The rule.** Every numeric custom property that any script, probe or reviewer
41	reads must be declared:
42	
43	```css
44	@property --tx     { syntax: '<number>'; inherits: true; initial-value: 0; }
45	@property --slit-p { syntax: '<number>'; inherits: true; initial-value: 0; }
46	```
47	
48	Declare it when the property is created, not when a measurement fails. If you
49	are reading a property that is not declared, **that is the finding** — declare
50	it first, then measure.
51	
52	**The check that proves the check:** run `parseFloat(getComputedStyle(el)
53	.getPropertyValue('--tx'))` against the *current, undeclared* state first. It
54	must return `NaN`. A version of this check that returns a number against both a
55	declared and an undeclared property is measuring nothing.
56	
57	### M2 · Never judge an act in a preview mode
58	
59	A `?preview=<name>` mode is a convenience that lands the page at a scroll
60	position. It is **not** evidence that the act renders correctly at that
61	position, and it drifts silently the moment the act's scroll window changes.
62	
63	**What it cost:** when plan 067 recomputed the act's window from hard-coded
64	numbers to calculated ones, every preview mode kept aiming at the old window. At
65	`tes-till-ritning-3` the sheet sat **1329 px below the viewport**. Every review
66	that had used the preview modes since — Astra's included — had been judging the
67	wrong scroll position.
68	
69	**The rule.** Before you judge an act from a preview mode, prove the mode lands
70	where it claims: read the element's bounding box against the viewport in that
71	mode and assert the overlap you expect. Failing that, **measure in real wheel
72	scroll** — `mouse.wheel`, 20 px steps, both directions — and say in your report
73	which method you used.
74	
75	### M3 · Every geometric check proves itself against a broken variant first
76	
77	Run each structural check **against a deliberately broken build** before you run
78	it against the real one. A check that returns green against both a broken and a
79	correct page measures nothing, and it will do so quietly, forever.

82	two of her own probe versions in r21 for exactly this reason, and rebuilt her

86	*"`.chapter-plate{clip-path:none;height:+900px}` → N hits, clean build → 0."*
87	A check reported without its broken-case value is not evidence and may not be
88	cited as one.

103	rule outlives the fix: **any surface a human uses to judge work must be

106	If you are ever handed a review surface and cannot state its cache behaviour,
107	assume it is lying to you until you have force-reloaded it once.

# Chain discipline

**Resident. Not routed.** This file loads with `SKILL.md` and is read by every
builder, every reviewer and every orchestrator in this chain, on every job.
It is the one document that is about *us* rather than about the page.

It exists because of a five-day run (Alunix V3d, 2026-09-15 → 09-20) that spent
**37 build rounds on 10 orders**, cost $24 for the last round alone, and ended
with the owner's verdict:

> *"resten av ändringarna motsvarade inte riktigt heller mina förväntningar även
> om de utfördes på papper."*
> — Anton, 2026-09-20

Nothing in that run failed for lack of craft. Every ordered point was built and
rendered. It failed because **the chain lied to itself five times and believed
each lie** — and every lie became a build round before anyone caught it. The
rules below are those five lies and their fixes, plus the four method changes
that came out of the same run.

**The rule everything else serves:** *a measurement you have not proven against
a known-broken case is not a measurement, it is a guess with a number on it.*

---

## 1 · Measurement

### M1 · Register every custom property before you read it

`getPropertyValue('--tx')` on an **unregistered** custom property returns the
token stream — `clamp(0,calc((0.3214 - 0.2258) / 0.1613),1)` — not a number.
`parseFloat` on that is `NaN`, and `NaN` silently compares as `0` in every filter
and every `if`.

**What it cost:** the `--slit-p` filter was inert through round 18 *and* through
two of Astra's review passes without anyone noticing. It then convinced the lead
that a colour draw had not started when `--tx` was in fact `0.59`, and that
false reading was written up as a finding before it was caught.

**The rule.** Every numeric custom property that any script, probe or reviewer
reads must be declared:

```css
@property --tx     { syntax: '<number>'; inherits: true; initial-value: 0; }
@property --slit-p { syntax: '<number>'; inherits: true; initial-value: 0; }
```

Declare it when the property is created, not when a measurement fails. If you
are reading a property that is not declared, **that is the finding** — declare
it first, then measure.

**The check that proves the check:** run `parseFloat(getComputedStyle(el)
.getPropertyValue('--tx'))` against the *current, undeclared* state first. It
must return `NaN`. A version of this check that returns a number against both a
declared and an undeclared property is measuring nothing.

### M2 · Never judge an act in a preview mode

A `?preview=<name>` mode is a convenience that lands the page at a scroll
position. It is **not** evidence that the act renders correctly at that
position, and it drifts silently the moment the act's scroll window changes.

**What it cost:** when plan 067 recomputed the act's window from hard-coded
numbers to calculated ones, every preview mode kept aiming at the old window. At
`tes-till-ritning-3` the sheet sat **1329 px below the viewport**. Every review
that had used the preview modes since — Astra's included — had been judging the
wrong scroll position.

**The rule.** Before you judge an act from a preview mode, prove the mode lands
where it claims: read the element's bounding box against the viewport in that
mode and assert the overlap you expect. Failing that, **measure in real wheel
scroll** — `mouse.wheel`, 20 px steps, both directions — and say in your report
which method you used.

### M3 · Every geometric check proves itself against a broken variant first

Run each structural check **against a deliberately broken build** before you run
it against the real one. A check that returns green against both a broken and a
correct page measures nothing, and it will do so quietly, forever.

**What it cost:** it has happened three times in this project. Astra discarded
two of her own probe versions in r21 for exactly this reason, and rebuilt her
column probe in r22 after a false negative.

**The rule.** Every check ships with its injected fault, named in the report:
*"`.chapter-plate{clip-path:none;height:+900px}` → N hits, clean build → 0."*
A check reported without its broken-case value is not evidence and may not be
cited as one.

---

## 2 · Verification

### V1 · A review surface never caches

**What it cost:** `board.py` sent only `Last-Modified`, no cache headers. Chrome
applied heuristic freshness and served a previous round without revalidating.
The owner reviewed stale code **at least twice**, concluded nothing had been
built, and had to ask *"är det ens något gjort?"* — a reasonable conclusion from
what he was actually looking at.

Fixed in `scripts/board.py` (`Cache-Control: no-store, must-revalidate`). The
rule outlives the fix: **any surface a human uses to judge work must be
uncacheable, and must say so in a header, not in a hope.**

If you are ever handed a review surface and cannot state its cache behaviour,
assume it is lying to you until you have force-reloaded it once.

### V2 · Verify in the render, not in the bytes

**What it cost:** the lead grepped the served cell over HTTP, found the change,
and reported *"ändringarna finns"* — while the owner was looking at a page that
did not have it. Bytes on a server prove nothing about what a browser paints.

**The rule.** "It is in the file" is not a verification. "It is in the response
body" is not a verification. The verification is **a rendered image of the page
the human will actually open**, read as an image, by the person making the claim.
When the two disagree, the render wins, and the discrepancy is itself the finding.

---

## 3 · Orchestration

### O1 · Run Codex directly, never through a wrapper agent

`Agent(codex-review)` cost **305,000 Opus tokens per round**. Inside that, the
actual Codex call was **one request, 24 images in, 6.3 kB of text out** — billed
to the OpenAI quota, not to ours. The other ~300k was an Opus subagent
re-doing the measurement work before asking the question.

**The rule.** Drive `codex exec` from the shell. `scripts/astra.py` takes a
prompt file, a screenshot glob and an output path, and reads the answer back.
Screenshots come from a capture script; the prompt comes from you; the verdict
costs almost nothing.

**What you must NOT drop along with the wrapper.** The wrapper verified every
Codex finding against the file and the pixels before releasing it. In r21, three
of Codex's four findings fell to that check. **The verification step is
mandatory and it is now yours.** A Codex verdict is a draft, never a finding.

`astra.py` refuses two failure modes by construction and both matter: an empty
response is an **error**, not "no findings"; and more than ~28 images produces
sludge, so the selection must be narrowed rather than padded.

### O2 · A plan that is not on disk does not exist

**What it cost:** an architect subagent reported a complete plan **three times**
without being able to save it, and said so only when asked for the files
directly. A builder was nearly dispatched against a plan that was never written.

**The rule.** `subagent_type: Plan` is read-only. Before any builder is
dispatched, **`Read` the plan file from disk and confirm it is the plan you
think it is.** A plan reported in a message is a draft. The artifact is the file.

Same rule for reference baselines, målbilder and captured screenshots: if the
path cannot be opened right now, it is not an input.

---

## 4 · Review

### R1 · Aesthetic review is a sanctioned mode

This is the single largest method gain in the run, and it was nearly lost.

`agents/codex-review.md` was written for code and measurements. In r23 it was
instead given the mandate *"varför är detta fult, och vad skulle göra det
vackert"*, with the customer's rejection treated as correct by definition and the
reviewer instructed to find **what it had missed**. The result was the best
review in the project's history. Astra wrote, in plain terms:

> *"Jag mätte att den klippta rektangeln äger 44 % av viewporten och kallade det
> 'en hel yta som förändras'. Jag mätte formens area och tog den för närvaro."*

...and then produced a direction a builder could draw from, rather than a defect
list.

**The rule.** When the owner rejects work that passed every gate, the failure is
not in the gates — it is that no one was asked the aesthetic question. Dispatch
Astra in **`mode: aesthetic`**, with these framings:

- The customer has already judged it and the customer is right by definition.
  Your job is not to defend the work; it is to find what you failed to see.
- Name *why* it is ugly in the terms of form — area, weight, rhythm, contrast,
  what owns the viewport — not in adjectives.
- Weight the answer in `fidelity` and `ceiling`. An aesthetic pass whose output
  is a defect list has failed at its one job.

**What this does not license.** An aesthetic pass may not re-choose the palette,
the type or the direction — that is still a Step 2 decision and still a
gate-order violation. It judges how well the *committed* direction is executed,
and where the execution reads as empty. The distinction is exact: **"this is
badly executed against its own intent" is a finding; "it would look better as
something else" is not.**

### R2 · A rule in prose needs a mechanical test

**What it cost:** F-018 (*the page never narrates itself*) was written into
`FEEDBACK.md`, `anti-patterns.md`, `gates.md`, `copy-gate.md` and
`production-tells.md` — and then broken by the very next sentence the chain
delivered:

> *"Vi har ingen husstil. Formen kommer ur verksamheten, och därför valde vi de
> två projekt som ligger längst ifrån varandra."*

New words, same posture. The sentence explains **the page's own selection** to
the reader; nobody asked why those two examples are on the page. It passed the
scanner because the rule was written for microtext and this was set in body size.

**The rule.** Every copy rule that names a *shape* rather than a word gets a
mechanical check, or it will be broken by the next fluent paragraph. F-018's
check is `scripts/self_reference_scan.py`: it flags every sentence whose subject
is the page, the section, the example or the selection. Run it on the rendered
copy, and run it against the sentence above first — it must flag it.

A prose rule with no test is a preference, and preferences lose to fluency.

---

## 5 · The round ladder

The five rules above stop the chain lying. This one stops the spiral.

**37 rounds for 10 orders** was not a speed problem. It was that **no round was
ever allowed to finish before the next one started.** Round 23 built nine ordered
points and never ran its own § Verification; the nine were then judged
"executed on paper" and the level not reached, which is the only verdict possible
when nobody checked.

**The ladder, in order, no skipping:**

1. **Plan on disk** (O2). Read it before dispatching.
2. **Build one round.**
3. **Verify that round completely** — its own plan's § Verification, all of it,
   not the parts that fit the remaining budget. Disk space, quota and time are
   not verification exemptions; if they run out, the round is **incomplete**, and
   that is what gets reported.
4. **Only then** does the next round start.

**A round may not be retro-fitted.** If round N's verification reveals a fault,
the fix is round N+1 — never a silent edit folded into round N+2's build.

**And the reporting rule that follows from all of it:** a round whose images
nobody has looked at has not been verified, whatever the log says. Do not report
a build as done on the strength of a green exit code. The builder reporting
"grinden grön" while the lead's own reading found a new fault is not a rare
event — it happened in r20 and r22 of this run.

---

## 6 · Where these rules are enforced

| Rule | Written into | Mechanised by |
|---|---|---|
| M1 register properties | this file | the `@property` block; check returns `NaN` on undeclared |
| M2 preview modes | this file | bounding-box assertion, or wheel scroll |
| M3 broken-variant first | this file · `design-verify` | every probe ships its injected fault |
| V1 no caching | this file | `scripts/board.py` `Cache-Control` |
| V2 render not bytes | this file · `agents/design-critic.md` | the review contract's `recapture` disposition |
| O1 Codex direct | this file · `agents/codex-review.md` | `scripts/astra.py` |
| O2 plan on disk | this file | `Read` the file before dispatch |
| R1 aesthetic mode | this file · `agents/codex-review.md` | `mode: aesthetic` in the dispatch |
| R2 rule needs a test | this file · `copy-gate.md` | `scripts/self_reference_scan.py` |

evidence, the chain's own measurement is a claim, and an unverified round is not
finished — it is unfinished, and says so.*

def main() -> None:
    if L.disabled():
        return
    event = L.read_event()
    tool = L.tool_name(event)

    # Generated material is a skill call like any other and gets measured like
    # one. Before this, a Higgsfield call left no trace at all: the ledger
    # could tell you which reference the builder read and not that it had spent
    # 17.5 credits on a clip (T12, 2026-09-08).
    if L.is_generation_tool(tool):
        root = L.project_root({"cwd": event.get("cwd")})
        L.log(root, event="generation", **L.generation_fields(event))
        return

    mcp_server = _mcp_server(tool)
    if mcp_server:
        root = L.project_root({"cwd": event.get("cwd")})
        L.log(root, event="mcp", server=mcp_server, **_mcp_fields(tool, event))
        return

    if tool != "Read":
        return
    path = L.target_file(event)
    if not path:
        return

    # cwd-based root, NOT project_root(event) — a SKILL.md or catalogue file
    # always lives in the shared skills directory or the catalogue (often
    # under an OneDrive/vault tree, or this repo, with its own .git), never
    # necessarily inside the project being built. Resolving root from the
    # file path here would file the read into the wrong ledger, so
    # design-stop.py / design-gate.py would never see it.
    root = L.project_root({"cwd": event.get("cwd")})

    skill = _skill_read(path)
    if skill:
        L.log(root, event="skill-read", skill=skill, file=path)

    ref = _classify_ref(path, root)
    if ref:
        L.log(root, event="ref-read", **ref)

    if not path.lower().endswith(IMAGE_EXTS):
        return

    # Images inside a catalogue entry (entries/<slug>/*.png) match `ref`
    # above AND still count toward the exit bar's vision requirement — the
    # reference floor and the "were the pixels ever looked at" check are
    # independent concerns, so both log unconditionally.
    cwd_root = root
    file_root = L.project_root(event)
    L.log(cwd_root, event="vision", file=path)
    if file_root != cwd_root:
        L.log(file_root, event="vision", file=path)

1	# TASTE.md — Antons smakprofil, läst ur katalogen
2	
3	Skriven 2026-09-04 av Claude efter egen läsning av alla 89 källor (55 råa skärmbilder Anton
4	sparat själv, 34 Refero-exporter) som bilder och text. Anteckningarna bakom:
5	`taste/notes-raw-read.md`, `taste/notes-refero-read.md`. Profilen beskriver **harmonin**, hur
6	typ, bild, yta och rörelse förhåller sig till varandra, inte vilka färger eller typsnitt som
7	ska användas. Färg och typsnitt härleds fortfarande ur varumärket (Tier 0–2); det här säger
8	hur de ska *samspela* när de väl är valda, och vad som aldrig får hända.
9	
10	Hur den används: `design/SKILL.md` Step 1b läser den när beställaren är Anton eller när
11	briefen saknar referenser. Reference-lockens preserve-lista prövas mot avsnitt 4.
12	Bake-offens riktningar seedas ur avsnitt 3.
13	
14	---
15	
16	## 1. Det genomgående temat: en auktoritet per sida
17	
18	Varje sparad sida låter **en enda sak** bära uppmärksamheten, och allt annat drar sig
19	tillbaka för den. Det är den enskilt tydligaste regeln i materialet, och den håller tvärs alla
20	kategorier:
21	
22	| Auktoriteten | Då gör typen | Då gör bilden | Då gör ytan | Exempel |
23	|---|---|---|---|---|
24	| **Typen** (ordmärke eller rubrik i viewport-bredd) | 100–265 px, en vikt, stram | tyst: liten, bredvid, eller bakom typen som ett lager | flat papper eller flat färgblock | Garden Eight, Shelby Kay, SpringSummer, Busy Bee, Indoek, Studio Ag, Mattis, Magnetism |
25	| **Fotot** (fullbleed, mörkt eller överexponerat) | vikt 300, ljus, stor men luftig, lägger sig i fotots mörka del | allt | ingen: fotot är ytan | Squarespace, Planhat, Apollo, Amrit, Montoni, Geon, Rogo, Diamond Rose |
26	| **Ytan/materialet** (papper, linne, terrakotta, celadon) | medelstor, gärna serif, får ta plats men inte skrika | plates bredvid texten, aldrig under | bär allt: ton-på-ton, hårlinjer, inga skuggor | Raus, Beautiful, Palais, TOMO, alet, Miti, Caractère Bois, Kinhive |
27	| **Produkten** (objektet ofriat i mitten) | uppercase 500 i små grader, eller helt tyst | ett objekt i tomrum | mörk eller flat | ORYZO, Busy Bee, Hungry Tiger, Aarke, David, Altitude |
28	| **Rörelsen** | tyst | tyst eller suddig | ljus, luftig | Perplexity, dope.security, alet, Bumble, Comet |
29	
30	Sidor där två av dessa konkurrerar finns inte i materialet. Det är därför Antons "för
31	snarlika"-kritik träffar de kedjebyggen som la stor serif *och* starkt foto *och* accentfärg
32	i samma fold: tre auktoriteter är ingen.
33	
34	**Regel:** namnge auktoriteten innan koden. Allt som inte är auktoriteten går ner ett steg
35	i vikt, storlek eller mättnad.
36	
37	## 2. Fem relationer som återkommer
38	
39	1. **Tyst typ ↔ stark bild, stark typ ↔ tyst bild.** Weight 300 vid 64–110 px sitter alltid på
40	   ett foto eller ett tomt papper. Fet eller kondenserad display (Busy Bee 238 px, Shelby Kay
41	   265 px) sitter alltid på en flat yta. Undantaget som håller: tung grotesk *genom* ett orört
42	   foto (Indoek, What Matters, Go RVing, Mattis), men bara när typen är tung nog att tåla
43	   fotot. Tunn typ på ett ljust, brusigt foto förekommer noll gånger.
44	2. **Ett papper, en accent.** 69 av 89 har en varm eller kall "paper"-yta och exakt en
45	   kromatisk färg som gör en sak: CTA, understryk, ordmärke. Vit yta är sällsynt (Paper,
46	   Not Real, Andre Candido, Aarke) och då är den *varmvit* och typen är svart. Två accenter
47	   förekommer bara i consumer/playful (OLIPOP, Palais, Shepherd).
48	3. **Struktur med hårlinjer och ton-på-ton, aldrig med kort.** Skuggade kort: 0 av 89 där
49	   Anton valt (de finns i tre AI-mallar, som defaults). Djup kommer av cream-på-cream,

# TASTE.md — Antons smakprofil, läst ur katalogen

Skriven 2026-09-04 av Claude efter egen läsning av alla 89 källor (55 råa skärmbilder Anton
sparat själv, 34 Refero-exporter) som bilder och text. Anteckningarna bakom:
`taste/notes-raw-read.md`, `taste/notes-refero-read.md`. Profilen beskriver **harmonin**, hur
typ, bild, yta och rörelse förhåller sig till varandra, inte vilka färger eller typsnitt som
ska användas. Färg och typsnitt härleds fortfarande ur varumärket (Tier 0–2); det här säger
hur de ska *samspela* när de väl är valda, och vad som aldrig får hända.

Hur den används: `design/SKILL.md` Step 1b läser den när beställaren är Anton eller när
briefen saknar referenser. Reference-lockens preserve-lista prövas mot avsnitt 4.
Bake-offens riktningar seedas ur avsnitt 3.

---

## 1. Det genomgående temat: en auktoritet per sida

Varje sparad sida låter **en enda sak** bära uppmärksamheten, och allt annat drar sig
tillbaka för den. Det är den enskilt tydligaste regeln i materialet, och den håller tvärs alla
kategorier:

| Auktoriteten | Då gör typen | Då gör bilden | Då gör ytan | Exempel |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Typen** (ordmärke eller rubrik i viewport-bredd) | 100–265 px, en vikt, stram | tyst: liten, bredvid, eller bakom typen som ett lager | flat papper eller flat färgblock | Garden Eight, Shelby Kay, SpringSummer, Busy Bee, Indoek, Studio Ag, Mattis, Magnetism |
| **Fotot** (fullbleed, mörkt eller överexponerat) | vikt 300, ljus, stor men luftig, lägger sig i fotots mörka del | allt | ingen: fotot är ytan | Squarespace, Planhat, Apollo, Amrit, Montoni, Geon, Rogo, Diamond Rose |
| **Ytan/materialet** (papper, linne, terrakotta, celadon) | medelstor, gärna serif, får ta plats men inte skrika | plates bredvid texten, aldrig under | bär allt: ton-på-ton, hårlinjer, inga skuggor | Raus, Beautiful, Palais, TOMO, alet, Miti, Caractère Bois, Kinhive |
| **Produkten** (objektet ofriat i mitten) | uppercase 500 i små grader, eller helt tyst | ett objekt i tomrum | mörk eller flat | ORYZO, Busy Bee, Hungry Tiger, Aarke, David, Altitude |
| **Rörelsen** | tyst | tyst eller suddig | ljus, luftig | Perplexity, dope.security, alet, Bumble, Comet |

Sidor där två av dessa konkurrerar finns inte i materialet. Det är därför Antons "för
snarlika"-kritik träffar de kedjebyggen som la stor serif *och* starkt foto *och* accentfärg
i samma fold: tre auktoriteter är ingen.

**Regel:** namnge auktoriteten innan koden. Allt som inte är auktoriteten går ner ett steg
i vikt, storlek eller mättnad.

## 2. Fem relationer som återkommer

1. **Tyst typ ↔ stark bild, stark typ ↔ tyst bild.** Weight 300 vid 64–110 px sitter alltid på
   ett foto eller ett tomt papper. Fet eller kondenserad display (Busy Bee 238 px, Shelby Kay
   265 px) sitter alltid på en flat yta. Undantaget som håller: tung grotesk *genom* ett orört
   foto (Indoek, What Matters, Go RVing, Mattis), men bara när typen är tung nog att tåla
   fotot. Tunn typ på ett ljust, brusigt foto förekommer noll gånger.
2. **Ett papper, en accent.** 69 av 89 har en varm eller kall "paper"-yta och exakt en
   kromatisk färg som gör en sak: CTA, understryk, ordmärke. Vit yta är sällsynt (Paper,
   Not Real, Andre Candido, Aarke) och då är den *varmvit* och typen är svart. Två accenter
   förekommer bara i consumer/playful (OLIPOP, Palais, Shepherd).
3. **Struktur med hårlinjer och ton-på-ton, aldrig med kort.** Skuggade kort: 0 av 89 där
   Anton valt (de finns i tre AI-mallar, som defaults). Djup kommer av cream-på-cream,
   1 px-linjer, överlapp och färgband som byter *material* mellan sektioner.
4. **Storlekskontrast 5–15×, inte 2–3×.** Display 64–265 px mot body 14–17 px. En sida med
   "h1 48 / h2 32 / p 16" finns inte i materialet. Mellanrubriker är antingen små uppercase
   kickers (11–13 px, tracking 0.1–0.2 em) eller lika stora som display. Mellanläget saknas.
5. **Rundning är ett beslut.** Antingen 0–3 px (Amrit, Apollo, alet, Not Real, Squarespace,
   NGLM) eller stor och avsiktlig (Raus 20/40, Bumble 16–24, pill-knappar 999). Ingen ligger
   på 8 px-default.

## 3. Per kategori: harmonin, och vad som bär

Kategorierna är de i `categories.md`. "Bär" = auktoriteten enligt avsnitt 1.

### product-focused (SaaS, verktyg)
Bär: **fotot som stämning** (Planhat, Sanity, Rogo, HappyRobot) eller **produkten som bild**
(Paper, Solva, customer.io, Operator). Typ: neo-grotesk 300–400 i stor grad, stram tracking,
eller en två-tons rubrik (Paper: mörk första rad, grå fortsättning). Ytan: mörk eller varmvit,
aldrig lila. Rörelse: subtil, aldrig "breathing". Siffror som textur (Hark, RRE, NGLM) i
display-grad med liten etikett, ruled. **Det Anton avvisar här:** feature-grid med ikoner,
"trusted by"-logg-rad som fyllning, tre lika kort. I mallarna han sparat (Nura, Solva, Areto)
är det heron han sparat, inte resten.

### portfolio / studio
Bär: **typen som verket.** Ordmärke eller påstående i viewport-bredd (Magnetism, Garden
Eight, Studio Ag, Mattis, Example, Orix). Arbetet i asymmetriskt grid, metadata i marginalen
(mono eller 11 px uppercase). Ingen CTA-fyllning; kontakt är en textrad. Ytan: papper eller
flat färgblock; Mattis och Lucci visar att ett helt orange eller rött band är tillåtet när
typen är tung grotesk.

### institutional
Bär: **lugn skala.** Få enheter, stor luft, en sats i taget (Hark, RRE, Montoni, Equity Fund).
Typ: grotesk 300–400 eller en lugn serif, aldrig kondenserad. Data som textur är kategorins
signatur. Foto: landskap eller material, mörkat. Rörelse: nästan ingen.

### editorial
Bär: **ytan + rytmen.** Papper, kolumner, kickers, plates bredvid texten, journal-rytm (Raus,
Indoek, Caractère Bois, Dovetail, Redbrick, Aevi). Serif tillåten och vanlig, men alltid med
en grotesk eller mono för etiketter, aldrig serif på etiketter.

### hospitality / plats
Bär: **fotot.** Typen anpassar sig: ljus 300-serif *i* fotots mörka del (Amrit, Apollo,
Montoni, Geon) eller display-serif på papper *bredvid* fotot (Raus, Miti, Diamond Rose).
Alltid en enda handling (boka/sök) i en enda färg. Ordmärke i viewport-bredd är vanligt
(Diamond Rose, Maloot, Miti-kurvan).

### consumer-brand
Bär: **produkten och färgen.** Flat färgblock, produkten ofriad i mitten, condensed/fet
display 100–240 px (Busy Bee, Hungry Tiger, David, Lucci, Deon Libra). Marquee-remsan som
avdelare hör hit och ingen annanstans. Färgen får vara lek; typen är sign-painting.

### luxury-craft
Bär: **ett objekt i tomrum.** Cream-typ, uppercase 500 i små grader, allt annat tyst (ORYZO,
Diabla, Dix Hectares, Aarke, Geon). Material före dekor: sten, kork, linne, stål.

### playful
Bär: **färgen eller rörelsen** (Bumble, OLIPOP, Palais, Andre Candido). Illustration bara som
teckning eller 3D-objekt, aldrig som ikon-set. Två accenter tillåtna, inte tre.

## 4. Beslutsregler för typsnitt och bild, så att de samspelar

Dessa är de regler kedjan ska pröva varje val mot. De gäller *utöver* varumärkets egna
tokens.

1. **Välj auktoritet först, typsnitt sedan.** Bär fotot: välj ett snitt som tål vikt 300 i
   80 px (neo-grotesk eller en serif med låg kontrast). Bär typen: välj ett snitt med
   karaktär i 150 px+ (kondenserad grotesk, didone, eller ett ovanligt display-serif) och
   håll fotot litet. Bär ytan: en lugn serif i 40–70 px och grotesk för allt annat.
2. **Två snitt, aldrig tre, och rollerna korsar aldrig.** Ett för röst (display + body eller
   bara display), ett för register (etiketter, siffror, nav). Mono får bara vara register.
   Serif får aldrig vara etikett.
3. **Bilden väljs efter hur mycket typ den ska bära.** Typ över foto kräver antingen ett
   mörkt/överexponerat parti där typen får stå (mät kontrasten under den ljusaste ramen,
   Step 5), eller en typvikt ≥ 700. Annars läggs fotot bredvid texten som en plate med
   caption. Aldrig scrim över hela bilden som räddning.
4. **Ett papper, en accent, och accenten gör en sak.** Bestäm vad (CTA, understryk,
   ordmärke, en siffra) och låt den inte göra något annat. Andra accenten kräver kategori
   consumer/playful och en motivering i beslutsledgern.
5. **Sektioner byter material, inte bara bakgrund.** När sidan behöver en ny akt: helt
   färgband, mörk-till-ljus inversion, eller papper-till-foto. Inte "grå sektion".
6. **Kontrast i skala, inte i vikt.** Display minst 5× body. Mellanrubriker antingen som
   kickers (små, tracking) eller lika stora som display. Aldrig en 32 px-mellannivå.
7. **Djup utan skugga.** Hårlinjer, ton-på-ton, överlapp, inversion. Skugga bara på en
   flytande komponent (modal, sökfält) och då knappt synlig.
8. **Rörelse bara där typ och bild är tysta.** Är auktoriteten typ eller foto: reveal och
   pin räcker. Är auktoriteten rörelsen: låt typen vara 300 och bilden suddig.
   *Precisering (r6, 2026-09-06):* när briefen uttryckligen ber om scrollkoreografi är
   rörelsen auktoriteten **i set-piece-akten**: där viker typ och foto (typ i vikt 300,
   bilden får bli suddig eller resa), och resten av sidan följer regeln som den står.
   Utan den här raden läste byggarna regel 8 som skäl att hoppa över set-piecet helt.
   Läs också `FEEDBACK.md` bredvid den här filen: Antons domar, en regel per post.
9. **Siffror får vara textur bara om de är sanna.** Formen (display-grad, liten etikett,
   ruled) tas; innehållet måste vara systemets eget (Alunix-regeln).
10. **Ordmärket får vara heron.** Namnet i viewport-bredd, sloganen liten, är en fullt
    tillåten fold i den här profilen och ofta den starkaste.

## 5. Avvisat, med belägg

Förekomst i 89 sparade källor: ikongrid 0 · gradient-mesh 1 (Brand Federation, sparad för
heroformen) · glasmorfism 0 · centrerad hero med badge-rad 0 (utom AI-mallar) · lila/indigo-
accent 1 (dope.security, som glöd) · skuggade 8 px-kort 3 (alla mall-defaults) · stockfoto av
leende team 0 · "h1 48 / h2 32"-skala 0 · dekorativa blobbar 1 (Palais, handritade) ·
tre lika feature-kort 4 (alla i AI-mallar Anton sparat för heron).

Slutsats: det Anton *inte* har sparat är lika entydigt som det han sparat. Ett bygge som
innehåller något ur listan ovan ligger utanför profilen oavsett hur välgjort det är.

## 6. Den korta versionen (för Step 1b)

En auktoritet per sida. Tyst typ på stark bild, stark typ på tyst yta. Ett papper, en accent
som gör en sak. Hårlinjer och material, inte kort och skuggor. Skala 5× eller mer. Namnet får
vara heron. Sanna siffror som textur. Rörelse bara där allt annat är tyst.

317	  i Stockholm"), sidomenyer som listar stegrubriker i liten grå text, och små
318	  förklarande rader under rubriker i liten storlek ("Första steget är ett samtal om
319	  vad ni gör.").
320	- **Antons ord:** "All sån liten 'beskrivande' stiltypisk AI-text är härmed helt
321	  förbjuden och jag vill att designsystemet härmed aktivt arbetar emot det och kollar
322	  efter det i befintliga sidor."
323	- **Dom:** dåligt, generellt — inte begränsat till Alunix-cellen som visade det.
324	- **Regel:** ingen liten text vars enda jobb är att fylla, förklara det uppenbara,
325	  eller se designad ut. Testet: gör raden ett jobb läsaren behöver (identifierar,
326	  differentierar, lokaliserar eller möjliggör en handling), eller talar den bara om
327	  sidan/exemplet i mindre storlek än brödtexten? Det senare tas bort. Antons uttryckliga
328	  undantag: en sajts egen genre-apparat som är stilenlig OCH bär en funktion i den
329	  genren är inte utfyllnad — Calyx tidskriftsapparat (utgåva, löpnummer, plats-index)
330	  och Hōrais avsiktliga etiketter (rätt-namn, servis-nummer) identifierar verkliga
331	  saker på riktiga sajter i den genren; en digital byrås demo-sida i Alunix genre har
332	  ingen sådan licens.
333	- **Status:** portad till `anti-patterns.md` § Descriptive microtext (gate 99),
334	  `production-tells.md` gate 99, `gates.md`, SKILL.md § Apparatus (marknadssidor:
335	  default noll), kontroll `skills/design/scripts/microtext_scan.py`,
336	  `design-catalogue/MICROTEXT-AUDIT.md`.
337	
338	### F-017 · Prisliggarens displaystorlek är bara för siffror, inte för texten bredvid
339	- **Visades:** ingen board — samma session, prisliggarmönstret i katalogen
340	  (`house-physics.md` § Ledger, redan i bruk i Calyx/Hyperborea).
341	- **Antons ord (parafraserat i beställningen, samma dag):** displaystorlek i en
342	  priskolumn är bara för siffror (kompakta figurer som bildar rytm); text i samma
343	  kolumn ("Pris vid förfrågan") sätts ett steg mindre och linjeras mot siffrornas
344	  baslinje; en kontaktrad storleksätts som en handling, inte som en rubrik.
345	- **Dom:** regel, inte ett fel som redan visats — katalogens befintliga ledgers
346	  (Calyx, Hyperborea) skrevs redan så (siffra i display, valuta i kicker), men
347	  regeln stod inte skriven separat från valutaetiketten, så en textrad ("Pris vid
348	  förfrågan", "Kontakta oss") kunde av misstag ärva samma display-storlek som
349	  priset. Skrivs ner nu så nästa bygge inte chansar.
350	- **Regel:** i en ledger-rad bär enbart siffercellen display-storleken; en textcell i
351	  samma kolumn (`"Pris vid förfrågan"`, en enhet, en villkorstext) sätts ett
352	  typografiskt steg mindre än siffran och baslinjelinjeras mot den, aldrig
353	  samma storlek. En kontaktrad (telefon, mejl, boka-länk) storlekssätts som en
354	  handling — knapptext- eller länkstorlek — aldrig som en rubrik.
355	- **Status:** portad till `house-physics.md` § Ledger, never card grid, kontrollen
356	  `microtext_scan.py --price-ledger`.
