# Fault taxonomy — what the owner rejects, and why

**Read this before you review, and read it before you build.** `design-catalogue/FEEDBACK.md`
is the *log*: one verdict, one rule, in the order he gave them. This file is the *analysis*:
every pushback from the Alunix run (2026-09-15 → 09-21, ~34 orders and 18 verdicts) sorted by
**cause**, because the cause is what a reviewer has to recognise before the owner has to say it
again.

The distinction that matters most, and the reason this file exists:

> **Almost none of the owner's pushbacks are taste.** Sorting them by cause, they land in
> eleven classes. Ten of them are *measurable* — a ratio, a seam, an overlap, a scale step, a
> cadence, a second reading, a control that does not do what it says. Only one class is
> exploration, and treating exploration as a defect is its own failure mode.

A reviewer who reports "this feels off" has done the owner's job for him. A reviewer who
reports *which class* and *what it measures* has done theirs.

---

## 1 · Balance and proportion

Something occupies too much or too little space **relative to its neighbour**. Never an
absolute size — always a ratio.

- *"minska även den överdrivna storleken som adressen har just nu"*
- *"förstorar hela rutan för ritningen och låter Calyx ta upp större plats i rutan, utan lika
  mycket luft runt om"*
- *"Exempelcase-rubriken ligger för ensamt och tar alldeles för stor plats"*
- *"'Första steget är ett samtal om vad du gör.' är så litet att det försvinner helt mellan det
  andra"*
- *"texten för 'Pris vid förfrågan' och Kontakt är alldeles för stor och blir malplacerad"*

**Detect.** For each element, name the element it is competing with and give the ratio. "The
address is 2,4× the ledger numerals" is a finding. "The address feels big" is not. A list
where one item is at a different weight than its siblings is always this class — either match
it or promote it deliberately.

**Also here:** one authority per page (TASTE § 1). Two elements fighting for the same
attention is balance, not style.

## 2 · Transition and seam

The join between two acts is wrong — a hard edge where two grounds meet, or the frames *in
between* carry nothing.

- *"övergången från den blå sektionen till ritningen är fortfarande för trubbig med stora
  fyrkantiga block i flera scroll-lägen"*
- *"Fixa även övergången mellan det blå blocket och ritningen … nu är det extremt platt"*
- *"övergången till exempelcase är även väldigt dåligt gjord med en mörk ruta"*
- *"testa … skapa en snygg övergång från bilden med prissektionen"*

**Detect.** Two separate checks, and both are required:
1. **The seam itself.** Do two grounds meet at a visible line? Sweep the boundary in wheel
   scroll and read it. A tonal inversion must *blend* or be a *deliberate* hard edge — never
   an accidental one.
2. **The frames between.** Sweep the whole act at 20 px and count frames below the text
   floor. Measured on this run: **46 of 121 frames under 18 % text, lowest 1,5 %.** An empty
   frame is not a pause, it is the fault.

**Never fix a transition with a translucent overlay.** A veil at partial opacity has a
mid-state, and the mid-state is grey. This was diagnosed twice on this run — once on
`.chapter-plate`, once again when the same shape was reintroduced. A gradient has no
mid-state; a clocked veil does.

## 3 · Collision, clipping, fit

Elements touch, overlap, or are cut. Purely measurable.

- *"siffrorna går ihop med texterna"* — the step number and the small-caps label, on every step
- *"undersidan av 'Från samtal till lanserad sida.' klipps i underkant"* — the heading cut by
  its own stamp box
- *"Innehållet ryms inte heller på helsida utan klipps"*
- *"Lös även problemet med utrymmet på bokningssidan av Hōrai för att allt ska rymmas på
  enklast möjliga sätt"*
- *"Observera även kanterna på sidramarna, där det syns en tunn färgkant, lös det helt och
  hållet"*

**Detect.** Bounding boxes, not eyeballs. Minimum gap between adjacent elements; every text
block fully inside its container (watch descenders — a clipped descender is the classic);
nothing overflowing its section at any width. **Check the pair he actually named:** on this
run a probe measured number→paragraph (59 px, passing) while the collision was
number→*label*, which nothing measured. Measure the pair that is visually adjacent, not the
pair that was easy to select.

## 4 · Scale and hierarchy

Something sits at the wrong level, so the eye is not drawn where it should be.

- *"ögonen ska dras dit och läsa texten automatisk"*
- *"texten under texten lika stor"* — a sub-line should match the line it belongs to
- *"Gör även texten 'Berätta om er verksamhet' större och mer Impactful"*

**Detect.** TASTE § 4.6 is the rule and it is exact: **display at least 5× body; subheads are
either small kickers (tracking, 11–13 px) or display size — never the 32 px middle.** A
heading that is neither is in the forbidden zone, whatever it looks like. With 16 px body the
display floor is 80 px. Name the step; do not describe the feeling.

## 5 · Copy voice — the AI register

The writing reads as generated. This is the class he has had to repeat **three times**, which
makes it the most expensive one in the log.

- *"det verkar helt hjärndött, helt självklara saker som skriker AI eftersom att man antar att
  kunden är helt IQ-befriad"*
- *"är återigen helt hjärndött, och precis samma AI-slop som jag reagerade på tidigare,
  bekräfta att du förstår varför"*
- *"texten under rubriken är fortfarande fruktansvärd AI-slop, bekräfta att du förstått vad jag
  menar, det är väldigt tydligt"*
- *"rubrikerna för de båda casen lite roligare, nu känns de väldigt platta och intetsägande"*

**Detect — and this is the part that is always missed: the fault is the CADENCE, not the
words.** Rewriting the vocabulary while keeping the shape reproduces it exactly, which is what
happened on the second and third attempt. The shapes:

- **The roadmap.** A sentence describing the section's own disposition — what follows, in what
  order, and why. *"Vi går igenom vad vi valde i dem och varför."*
- **The disclaimer.** A caveat about the material's status, placed before the material.
  *"Ingen av dem finns."*
- **Setup → caveat → roadmap**, in that order. The default shape of "introduce a section".
- **The obvious stated.** Telling the reader something they already know, which reads as
  contempt for them.
- **The page narrating itself** (F-018). Any sentence whose subject is the page, the section,
  the example or the selection.

**Run the test, not the vibe:** `skills/design/scripts/self_reference_scan.py` — four
categories, with a `--selftest` that must pass first. A prose rule with no test gets broken by
the next fluent paragraph; that is measured, not theoretical.

## 6 · Ambiguity — the line that can be misread

- *"'Hōrai serverar bokningen sist.' är lätt att feltolka, serverar de bokningar i andra hand,
  är det bättre med 'serverar bokningen först' eller vad är motiveringen bakom?"*

**Detect.** Read the line as a stranger with no context, and write down the **second reading**.
If a plausible reading is wrong or embarrassing, the line is a finding — and the fix is to
state the intended meaning directly, not to add a clarifying clause. He asks for the
reasoning, so give it: *why* this wording and not the other.

## 7 · Broken affordance and semantic mismatch

A control, a state, or a label does not do what it says.

- *"Gör även så att man kommer till kontaktsidan om man klickar på 'Boka möte' på visitkortet
  längst upp"* — the CTA opened a mail client instead of reaching the section
- *"Calyx ska inte vara svartvit, den kan vara det under ritningsprocessen, men ska få sin färg
  i den färdiga versionen i sista steget"* — colour as a function of progress, wrongly mapped
- *"Hōrai är ett fönster i fasaden, inte en ruta utanpå den"* (F-010) — a compositing
  relationship the build got wrong

**Detect.** Trace every interactive element to its **actual effect**, not its label: click it
and watch where it goes. Trace every time-varying property to the state it encodes: is the
value mapped to the right thing at the right moment? This class is invisible in a static
screenshot and must be walked.

## 8 · Calibration — the middle he can only recognise

He oscillates, and the oscillation is the information.

- process copy: 35–44 words → 18–22 → *"Texten blev även aningen för kortfattad, försök
  återigen hitta en balans mellan den ursprungliga versionen i v3C och den nuvarande"* → 28–34
- *"Försök förkorta texterna utan att de blir så kortfattade som tidigare"*

**Detect.** This class is **not a defect** and must not be reported as one. The target is a
band, and the band is found by reading what the *previous* version was and landing between the
two. Two things make it tractable:
- **When he supplies a target sentence, it is the spec.** He did twice (*"observera skillnaden
  och försök applicera det på de övriga med samma ton"*). His example is the tone; measure the
  difference he names — shorter, merged clauses, ends in an image — and apply it to the rest.
- **Count words.** "Aningen för kortfattad" against a numbered previous version is a number,
  not a mood.

## 9 · Emptiness — a column with no weight

- *"just nu är det som en rullande paragraf och läser uppnår inte den slående effekt som
  förväntas"*
- *"stora tomma ytor"* — recurring, in several rounds

**Detect.** Measure ink coverage per frame and per column. **Weight every column you open**:
a rail holding two whispered lines beside a large block is a hole, not a rail. Either give it
something with presence (a display numeral, an image, a full-height rule) or close it and give
the content the width.

## 10 · Exploration — NOT a fault

This is the class that produces noise when it is misread as a defect.

- *"Motivera den valet till den vita bakgrunden för ritningen. Jag vill att du ber om en
  inverterad variant"*
- *"Testa att invertera den sektionen till svart"*
- *"testa att lägga en bild undertill under texten, bredvid formuläret"*
- *"Jag vill att du testar lägga processbeskrivningarna på vänster sida om ritningen"*

**The signals are the words *testa* and *motivera*.** He is interrogating a decision, not
reporting a defect. What he wants is **the reasoning and the alternative**, and sometimes he
wants to see both to choose. A reviewer that flags an exploration request as a fault has
misread the job — and a builder that *argues instead of testing* has too.

**Corollary:** when a test is ordered, the deliverable is the comparison, named as such.
Present the two states side by side and say what each buys. Then let him pick.

## 11 · Process and tooling — the chain, not the page

- *"ALLT är fortfarande exakt likadant som innan den senaste rundan, är det ens något gjort?"*
- *"ändringarna dyker upp i preview först, INNAN du gör något annat"*
- *"jag förväntar mig att se större resultat utan lika många försök den här gången"*

**Detect.** Not a page fault. Enforced in [`chain-discipline.md`](chain-discipline.md) § V1
(a review surface never caches) and § V2 (verify in the render, not in the bytes). The owner
concluded nothing had been built because the board served him a cached round — twice. When the
owner says "nothing changed", **suspect the surface before the build.**

---

## How to use this in a review

1. **Name the class.** "This is class 3, collision" beats "this feels tight". Six of the eleven
   classes are pure measurement; three more are structural reads; only two need judgment.
2. **Give the number or the name of the pair.** Every class above has a unit — a ratio, a gap
   in px, a frame count, a word count, a scale step, a second reading, a destination URL.
3. **Check the pair he named, not the pair that was convenient.** The 59 px probe measured
   number→paragraph while the collision was number→label. A check that measures the wrong pair
   returns green forever.
4. **Never report class 10 as a fault.** If the order contains *testa* or *motivera*, the
   finding is a comparison, not a defect.
5. **The three classes he repeats are 2, 3 and 5** — the seam, the collision, and the AI
   register. If a round touches a transition, a heading, or a lede, check those three first;
   that is where his rejections have actually landed, three times each.

**The one-line version:** *almost every pushback is a measurable relationship between two
things — and the reviewer's job is to name the two things before he has to.*

usage: select.py [-h] --brief BRIEF [--k K] [--exclude EXCLUDE] [--wildcard]
                 [--explain] [--json] [--root ROOT] [--dry-run]

select.py - pick the 2-4 catalogue entries a brief must be measured against.

Why this exists
---------------
r7 (2026-09-06/07) put the slugs straight into the builder prompt. The builders
read them, so the reference floor was satisfied, and `Skill(design-catalog)`
was still never invoked: the *selection* came out of the orchestrator's memory,
not out of the catalogue. Nothing could tell the difference afterwards.

This script is that difference. It scores every entry in index.json against the
brief's declared register / grammar / category / authority plus its free text,
prints a ranked list, and writes ONE `catalogue-select` row into the session
ledger naming the chosen slugs. design-gate.py's reference floor requires that
row before the first UI write, so a build cannot proceed on recalled references.

Deterministic. No model call anywhere in here.

    python scripts/catalogue/select.py --brief BRIEF.md [--k 4] [--wildcard]
                                       [--exclude slug,slug] [--explain] [--json]
                                       [--root DIR] [--dry-run]

options:
  -h, --help         show this help message and exit
  --brief BRIEF
  --k K
  --exclude EXCLUDE
  --wildcard         add one high-scoring entry from OUTSIDE the brief's
# V3g · godkända effekter (skyddade)

Varje effekt nedan har Anton bedömt som bra. En runda får inte ändra dem om briefen inte
uttryckligen säger det, och ingen av dem får bli sämre mätt med `section_probe.py`.
Baslinjen är `shots/section-probe-baseline.json`. Den skrivs när loopfixen är gjord, eftersom
dagens siffror bär loopens kostnad.

| Effekt | Var | Vad som är bra (Antons ord) | Signatur att hålla |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tesrubriken reser sig och står | `#tes`, `.tes-top` pin 0,9 vh + char-rise | "Det första intrycket är digitalt … var bättre" i V3f | p95 i `#tes` ≤ V3f-nivå (33 ms) utan loop; rubriken helt synlig ≥ 40 vh |
| Rubrikerna i allmänhet | alla `headline-40/50` | "rubrikerna blev mycket bättre" (V3f) | står stilla och hela ≥ 40 vh (motion.md läsregel) |
| Kontakten, kortet lämnas över | `#kontakt` | "även kontaktsidan" (V3f) | kortet vänder sig självt vid 0,7; heron speglad |
| Showcase-mekanismen | `#showcase` | "showcasen är bättre", "behåll mekanismen" (V3g R2) | en pin skapad en gång; övertoning mellan steg; räknare + mintspår |
| Övertoning vid casebyte | `activateCase` | ingen hård övergång (V3g R1–R2) | inget scrollY-hopp > baslinjen vid klick |

Underkänt, får inte återkomma: stegrubrik i displayskala och jättesiffra i rutan (F-019);
numerisk scrub och Lenis-standardtempo (F-020); refresh-loop via iframe-omladdning (F-021).

def read_brief(path: Path) -> dict:
    """Pull declared fields out of a brief, plus its free text.

    Accepts `Register: modern clean` and the markdown-bolded
    `**Register:** modern clean` the chain's own BRIEF template uses.
    """
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") if path.exists() else ""
    out = {"text": text}
    for key in ("register", "grammar", "category", "category2", "mode", "authority", "family"):
        m = re.search(r"^[#*\s]*" + key + r"\s*[:*]+\s*(.+)$", text, re.I | re.M)
        if m:
            out[key] = m.group(1).strip().strip("*_` ").lower()
    return out


def words(s):
    return set(w for w in re.findall(r"[a-zaaoAAO][a-zaao\-]{2,}", (s or "").lower())
               if w not in STOP)


def prior_primaries(repo: Path) -> set:
    """Slugs already used as a primary reference for this client. Reusing one
    is how two rounds end up looking like each other."""
    out = set()
    for brief in repo.glob("tests/alunix-*/**/BRIEF.md"):
        try:
            t = brief.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        except Exception:
            continue
        for m in re.finditer(r"^\s*[-*]?\s*Primary\s*[:*]+\s*([a-z0-9\-]+)", t, re.I | re.M):
            out.add(m.group(1).strip().lower())
    return out


# Product

<!-- impeccable:product-schema 1 -->

Källa: `tests/alunix-ab-r7/PROMPT.md`, avsnitten "Alunix, fakta", "Copy som ska användas
ordagrant" och "Förbjudet, bindande". Ingen annan källa har använts. Står det inte där står
det inte här.

## Platform

web

Belägg: de tre exempelsajterna är `.html`-filer under `/sites/` som serveras live och visas i
`<iframe>` från samma origin.

## Users

Vi vänder oss till verksamheter som behöver en webbplats. Sidan tilltalar dem i andra person,
"er" och "ni", aldrig "jag". De verksamhetstyper vi faktiskt kan visa upp är florist,
restaurang och konferens, eftersom det är vad de tre exempelsajterna är.

Vad de behöver av oss står i rubriken och ingen annanstans: `Er hemsida är nutidens
visitkort`. Vi vet alltså vad sidan lovar dem. Vi vet inte hur de köper, när de köper eller
vad de jämför med. Ingen intervju finns.

Ingen ytterligare målgrupp är bekräftad. Bransch, storlek och köpsituation är öppna frågor,
inte fakta.

## Product Purpose

Alunix är en webbyrå i Sverige. Sidan säljer en tjänst: webbdesign.

Vi skapar skräddarsydda webbplatser. Underraden löd ordagrant: `Vi skapar
skräddarsydda webbplatser som hjälper er att exponera verksamheten.`
**V3d, Antons beslut 2026-09-20: underraden är borttagen helt.** Heron bär på
rubriken och kortet. Låset gäller fortfarande V3c.

Erbjudandet är samlat: `Webbdesign, design och system. Allt på ett ställe.` Tjänsterna är tre
och numrerade 01 till 03: `Design`, `Utveckling`, `System`. Var och en får en kort underrad i
byråröst, utan påståenden om kunder eller resultat.

Tesrubriken är `VI BYGGER ERT VARUMÄRKE.`

Prisrubriken är `Alla har rätt till bra design.`

## Positioning

Vi visar vad vi kan i stället för att påstå det. Byrån visar sitt arbete genom tre riktiga
exempelsajter som ligger i samma repo och serveras live. De får visas live i `<iframe>`, samma
origin när sidan serveras från repo-roten, och de ska vara användbara när de är öppna. En
besökare kan alltså använda arbetet direkt på sidan, inte bara titta på en bild av det.

Tre saker till skiljer erbjudandet: design, utveckling och system kommer från samma ställe;
två av tre paket har ett pris utskrivet på sidan; och prislöftet är formulerat som en
principsats, `Alla har rätt till bra design.`

## Operating Context

- De tre exempelsajterna ligger i samma repo som sidan och serveras live därifrån.
- Ramarna är samma origin när sidan serveras från repo-roten.
- En ram som visats får aldrig transformeras eller tonas efteråt. Den ska gå att använda.
- Skärmbilder av de tre sajterna ligger i `assets/demo-calyx.webp`, `assets/demo-horai.webp`
  och `assets/demo-hyperborea.webp`.
- Logotypen ligger i `assets/logo-white.svg` och `assets/logo-black.svg` och får läggas inline.
- Allt material ligger i `assets/`. Inga egna Unsplash-anrop och ingen egen server.
- Servern är `python ~/.agents/skills/design/scripts/serve.py --port <port>` från repo-roten.
- Kontakt sker via e-post. Det finns inget formulär som skickar någonstans.
  **V3d, Antons beslut 2026-09-20:** låset hävt för V3d. Sidan får en egen
  kontaktsektion med formulär efter priserna. Ingen server tillkommer: knappen
  öppnar ett mejl till `kontakt@alunix.se` med fältens innehåll, så den gör det
  den säger. Gäller bara V3d.

## Capabilities and Constraints

**Tre paket.** Raderna och priserna är låsta och skrivs ordagrant:

| Paket | Pris |
|---|---|
| `Standardpaket. Webbplats med CMS för egna ändringar och en första SEO-optimering.` | `26 900 kr` |
| `Paket med bokningssystem, betalning och kunddatabas.` | `38 900 kr` |
| `Helt skräddarsydda lösningar för produktkataloger, specialbyggda system med mera` | `Pris vid förfrågan` |

**Tre tjänster.** `Design`, `Utveckling`, `System`, numrerade 01 till 03, en kort underrad var.

**En kontaktväg.** `kontakt@alunix.se`, både som text och som mailto. Inget formulär.
  **V3d:** se hävningen ovan. Adressen står kvar som alternativ väg in bredvid formuläret.

**Tre exempelsajter, live.** Se Evidence on Hand.

**Bindande begränsningar i allt vi bygger:**

- Inga påhittade tal, kunder, omdömen, citat, logotypväggar, stjärnor eller "nöjda kunder".
- Inga tankstreck i synlig text.
- Inget "jag".
- Inga foton som läses som "vårt kontor" eller "vårt team".
- Inga hexfärger och inga typsnitt hämtade ur någon annan färdig mall.

**Öppet, inte bestämt:** vad de tre tjänsternas underrader säger ordagrant. De ska vara korta
och i byråröst, men texten är inte skriven.

## Brand Commitments

**Namn.** Alunix. Ett förbjudet namn finns, se Absences.

**Röst.** Byråröst i vi-form. Korta satser. Fakta före adjektiv. Svenska. Inget "jag". Inga
tankstreck i synlig text.

**Låst copy, copy-gate.** Följande rader bevaras ordagrant och skrivs aldrig om:

- `Er hemsida är nutidens visitkort`
- `Vi skapar skräddarsydda webbplatser som hjälper er att exponera verksamheten.` (gäller V3c. I V3d borttagen på Antons uttryckliga beslut 2026-09-20: "ta bort den lilla texten vid visitkortet helt". Låst copy räknar därmed 11 synliga rader i V3d.)
- `VI BYGGER ERT VARUMÄRKE.` (gäller V3c. I V3d borttagen på Antons uttryckliga beslut 2026-09-19: tesbandet slutar på "Vi hjälper er att synas på rätt sätt.")
- `Webbdesign, design och system. Allt på ett ställe.`
- `Design`, `Utveckling`, `System`
- `Standardpaket. Webbplats med CMS för egna ändringar och en första SEO-optimering.`
- `26 900 kr`
- `Paket med bokningssystem, betalning och kunddatabas.`
- `38 900 kr`
- `Helt skräddarsydda lösningar för produktkataloger, specialbyggda system med mera`
- `Pris vid förfrågan`
- `Alla har rätt till bra design.`
- `kontakt@alunix.se`
- `Exempelsida: Calyx, florist i Stockholm`
- `Exempelsida: Hōrai, Asian fusion-koncept`
- `Exempelsida: Hyperborea, konferens i Lund`

(De tre bildtexterna gäller V3c. I V3d borttagna på Antons beslut 2026-09-19: liten beskrivande text är förbjuden, F-016. Ramens namn bärs av iframens `title`.)

**Logotyp.** `assets/logo-white.svg` och `assets/logo-black.svg`. Får läggas inline.

**Dagens register, som jämförelse och inte som lås.** Kall nästan svart `#17181B`. Blå
`#1E5E9C` bara för handling. Geist för rubrik, Inter för brödtext, JetBrains Mono för data.
Ett nytt koncept får avvika helt från det.

## Evidence on Hand

Detta är hela beviskassan. Inget annat får synas på sidan.

**Tre exempelsajter, live i `<iframe>`, med sina låsta bildtexter:**

| Sajt | Fil | Rad att använda |
|---|---|---|
| Calyx | `/sites/calyx.html` | `Exempelsida: Calyx, florist i Stockholm` |
| Hōrai | `/sites/horai.html` | `Exempelsida: Hōrai, Asian fusion-koncept` |
| Hyperborea | `/sites/hyperborea.html` | `Exempelsida: Hyperborea, konferens i Lund` |

De tre exempelsajterna är de enda kunder som får synas.

**Skärmbilder av dem:** `assets/demo-calyx.webp`, `assets/demo-horai.webp`,
`assets/demo-hyperborea.webp`.

**Tre paket med pris:** `26 900 kr`, `38 900 kr`, `Pris vid förfrågan`, med paketraderna
ordagrant som de står under Capabilities and Constraints.

**En adress:** `kontakt@alunix.se`, som text och som mailto.

**Logotypfiler:** `assets/logo-white.svg`, `assets/logo-black.svg`.

**Ordagrann copy:** hela listan under Brand Commitments.

## Absences Future Work Must Not Fabricate

Inget av det här finns i beviskassan. Det får därför aldrig uppstå i en design, en bildtext,
en platshållare eller en bildprompt:

- Kunder utöver de tre exempelsajterna.
- Omdömen, recensioner och "nöjda kunder".
- Citat från någon utanför sidan.
- Logotypväggar.
- Stjärnor och betyg.
- Ett team att visa upp. Personer, porträtt, namn, roller.
- Ett kontor att visa upp. Inga foton som läses som "vårt kontor" eller "vårt team".
- Antal år i branschen.
- Antal projekt, antal kunder, antal leveranser.
- Påhittade tal överhuvudtaget. De enda siffrorna vi har är `26 900 kr` och `38 900 kr`, och
  tjänsternas numrering 01 till 03.
- Namnet Klova. Det får aldrig förekomma.

## Product Principles

1. **Beviset ska gå att använda, inte bara ses.** De tre sajterna är riktiga och körs live på
   sidan. Ramar som visats förblir användbara.
2. **Varje siffra på sidan är en siffra vi kan stå för.** Vi har två priser och en numrering.
   Fler tal finns inte, så fler tal skrivs inte.
3. **Priset står framme.** Två paket har ett utskrivet pris. Det tredje säger `Pris vid
   förfrågan` och inget annat.
4. **En adress, inget formulär.** (**Hävt för V3d 2026-09-20**, se § ovan.) `kontakt@alunix.se` är hela kontaktvägen, som text och som
   mailto.
5. **Vi talar i vi-form och kort.** Fakta före adjektiv. Aldrig "jag".

Erbjudandet är samlat: `Webbdesign, design och system. Allt på ett ställe.` Tjänsterna är tre
och numrerade 01 till 03: `Design`, `Utveckling`, `System`. Var och en får en kort underrad i
byråröst, utan påståenden om kunder eller resultat.

Tesrubriken är `VI BYGGER ERT VARUMÄRKE.`

Prisrubriken är `Alla har rätt till bra design.`

## Positioning

Vi visar vad vi kan i stället för att påstå det. Byrån visar sitt arbete genom tre riktiga
exempelsajter som ligger i samma repo och serveras live. De får visas live i `<iframe>`, samma
origin när sidan serveras från repo-roten, och de ska vara användbara när de är öppna. En
besökare kan alltså använda arbetet direkt på sidan, inte bara titta på en bild av det.

Tre saker till skiljer erbjudandet: design, utveckling och system kommer från samma ställe;
två av tre paket har ett pris utskrivet på sidan; och prislöftet är formulerat som en
principsats, `Alla har rätt till bra design.`

## Operating Context

- De tre exempelsajterna ligger i samma repo som sidan och serveras live därifrån.
- Ramarna är samma origin när sidan serveras från repo-roten.
- En ram som visats får aldrig transformeras eller tonas efteråt. Den ska gå att använda.
- Skärmbilder av de tre sajterna ligger i `assets/demo-calyx.webp`, `assets/demo-horai.webp`
  och `assets/demo-hyperborea.webp`.
- Logotypen ligger i `assets/logo-white.svg` och `assets/logo-black.svg` och får läggas inline.
- Allt material ligger i `assets/`. Inga egna Unsplash-anrop och ingen egen server.
- Servern är `python ~/.agents/skills/design/scripts/serve.py --port <port>` från repo-roten.
- Kontakt sker via e-post. Det finns inget formulär som skickar någonstans.
  **V3d, Antons beslut 2026-09-20:** låset hävt för V3d. Sidan får en egen
  kontaktsektion med formulär efter priserna. Ingen server tillkommer: knappen
  öppnar ett mejl till `kontakt@alunix.se` med fältens innehåll, så den gör det
  den säger. Gäller bara V3d.

## Capabilities and Constraints

**Tre paket.** Raderna och priserna är låsta och skrivs ordagrant:

| Paket | Pris |
|---|---|
| `Standardpaket. Webbplats med CMS för egna ändringar och en första SEO-optimering.` | `26 900 kr` |
| `Paket med bokningssystem, betalning och kunddatabas.` | `38 900 kr` |
| `Helt skräddarsydda lösningar för produktkataloger, specialbyggda system med mera` | `Pris vid förfrågan` |

**Tre tjänster.** `Design`, `Utveckling`, `System`, numrerade 01 till 03, en kort underrad var.

**En kontaktväg.** `kontakt@alunix.se`, både som text och som mailto. Inget formulär.
  **V3d:** se hävningen ovan. Adressen står kvar som alternativ väg in bredvid formuläret.

**Tre exempelsajter, live.** Se Evidence on Hand.

**Bindande begränsningar i allt vi bygger:**

- Inga påhittade tal, kunder, omdömen, citat, logotypväggar, stjärnor eller "nöjda kunder".
- Inga tankstreck i synlig text.
- Inget "jag".
- Inga foton som läses som "vårt kontor" eller "vårt team".
- Inga hexfärger och inga typsnitt hämtade ur någon annan färdig mall.

**Öppet, inte bestämt:** vad de tre tjänsternas underrader säger ordagrant. De ska vara korta
och i byråröst, men texten är inte skriven.

## Brand Commitments

**Namn.** Alunix. Ett förbjudet namn finns, se Absences.

**Röst.** Byråröst i vi-form. Korta satser. Fakta före adjektiv. Svenska. Inget "jag". Inga
tankstreck i synlig text.

**Låst copy, copy-gate.** Följande rader bevaras ordagrant och skrivs aldrig om:

- `Er hemsida är nutidens visitkort`
- `Vi skapar skräddarsydda webbplatser som hjälper er att exponera verksamheten.` (gäller V3c. I V3d borttagen på Antons uttryckliga beslut 2026-09-20: "ta bort den lilla texten vid visitkortet helt". Låst copy räknar därmed 11 synliga rader i V3d.)
- `VI BYGGER ERT VARUMÄRKE.` (gäller V3c. I V3d borttagen på Antons uttryckliga beslut 2026-09-19: tesbandet slutar på "Vi hjälper er att synas på rätt sätt.")
- `Webbdesign, design och system. Allt på ett ställe.`
- `Design`, `Utveckling`, `System`
- `Standardpaket. Webbplats med CMS för egna ändringar och en första SEO-optimering.`
- `26 900 kr`
- `Paket med bokningssystem, betalning och kunddatabas.`
- `38 900 kr`
- `Helt skräddarsydda lösningar för produktkataloger, specialbyggda system med mera`
- `Pris vid förfrågan`
- `Alla har rätt till bra design.`
- `kontakt@alunix.se`
- `Exempelsida: Calyx, florist i Stockholm`
- `Exempelsida: Hōrai, Asian fusion-koncept`
- `Exempelsida: Hyperborea, konferens i Lund`

(De tre bildtexterna gäller V3c. I V3d borttagna på Antons beslut 2026-09-19: liten beskrivande text är förbjuden, F-016. Ramens namn bärs av iframens `title`.)

**Logotyp.** `assets/logo-white.svg` och `assets/logo-black.svg`. Får läggas inline.

**Dagens register, som jämförelse och inte som lås.** Kall nästan svart `#17181B`. Blå
`#1E5E9C` bara för handling. Geist för rubrik, Inter för brödtext, JetBrains Mono för data.
Ett nytt koncept får avvika helt från det.

## Evidence on Hand

Detta är hela beviskassan. Inget annat får synas på sidan.

**Tre exempelsajter, live i `<iframe>`, med sina låsta bildtexter:**

| Sajt | Fil | Rad att använda |
|---|---|---|
| Calyx | `/sites/calyx.html` | `Exempelsida: Calyx, florist i Stockholm` |
| Hōrai | `/sites/horai.html` | `Exempelsida: Hōrai, Asian fusion-koncept` |
| Hyperborea | `/sites/hyperborea.html` | `Exempelsida: Hyperborea, konferens i Lund` |

De tre exempelsajterna är de enda kunder som får synas.

**Skärmbilder av dem:** `assets/demo-calyx.webp`, `assets/demo-horai.webp`,
`assets/demo-hyperborea.webp`.

**Tre paket med pris:** `26 900 kr`, `38 900 kr`, `Pris vid förfrågan`, med paketraderna
ordagrant som de står under Capabilities and Constraints.

**En adress:** `kontakt@alunix.se`, som text och som mailto.

**Logotypfiler:** `assets/logo-white.svg`, `assets/logo-black.svg`.

**Ordagrann copy:** hela listan under Brand Commitments.

## Absences Future Work Must Not Fabricate

Inget av det här finns i beviskassan. Det får därför aldrig uppstå i en design, en bildtext,
en platshållare eller en bildprompt:

- Kunder utöver de tre exempelsajterna.
- Omdömen, recensioner och "nöjda kunder".
- Citat från någon utanför sidan.
- Logotypväggar.
- Stjärnor och betyg.
- Ett team att visa upp. Personer, porträtt, namn, roller.
- Ett kontor att visa upp. Inga foton som läses som "vårt kontor" eller "vårt team".
- Antal år i branschen.
- Antal projekt, antal kunder, antal leveranser.
- Påhittade tal överhuvudtaget. De enda siffrorna vi har är `26 900 kr` och `38 900 kr`, och
  tjänsternas numrering 01 till 03.
- Namnet Klova. Det får aldrig förekomma.

## Product Principles

1. **Beviset ska gå att använda, inte bara ses.** De tre sajterna är riktiga och körs live på
   sidan. Ramar som visats förblir användbara.
2. **Varje siffra på sidan är en siffra vi kan stå för.** Vi har två priser och en numrering.
   Fler tal finns inte, så fler tal skrivs inte.
3. **Priset står framme.** Två paket har ett utskrivet pris. Det tredje säger `Pris vid
   förfrågan` och inget annat.
4. **En adress, inget formulär.** (**Hävt för V3d 2026-09-20**, se § ovan.) `kontakt@alunix.se` är hela kontaktvägen, som text och som
   mailto.
5. **Vi talar i vi-form och kort.** Fakta före adjektiv. Aldrig "jag".

<!doctype html>
<html lang="sv">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1">
<title>Alunix · Digital byrå för design, utveckling och system</title>
<link rel="preload" href="assets/fonts/geist-500-latin.woff2" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="assets/vendor/lenis.css">

<style>
@font-face{
  font-family:"Geist";
  src:url("assets/fonts/geist-500-latin.woff2") format("woff2");
  font-weight:500; font-style:normal; font-display:swap;
}
@font-face{
  font-family:"Geist Mono";
  src:url("assets/fonts/geist-mono-400-latin.woff2") format("woff2");
  font-weight:400; font-style:normal; font-display:swap;
}

:root{
  --paper:#ffffff;
  --ink:#232323;
  --black:#000000;
  --grey:#d9d9d9;
  --mint:#0af474;
  --mint-soft:#a3fbcb;
  --rust:#9c5a3a;
  --lacquer:#b23524;
  /* R8: sekundär brödtext, ett värde per grund (8,9:1 på --paper, 11,8:1 på --black) */
  --ink-2:#4a4a4a;
  --paper-2:#bdbdbd;
  --seam:1px solid #000;

  --headline-50:clamp(3.25rem, 0.418rem + 12.082vw, 12.5rem);
  --headline-40:clamp(2.5rem, 1.352rem + 4.9vw, 6.25rem);
  --headline-20:clamp(2rem, 1.694rem + 1.306vw, 3rem);
  --h3:38px;
  --body:16px;
  --body-30:clamp(1.5rem, 1.347rem + 0.653vw, 2rem);
  --caption:13px;
  --cellpad:20px;
}

*{box-sizing:border-box;}
html{color-scheme:light;}
body{
  margin:0;
  background:#000;
  color:var(--ink);
  font-family:"Geist","Arial",system-ui,sans-serif;
  font-weight:500;
  line-height:1.3;
  -webkit-font-smoothing:antialiased;
  overflow-x:hidden;
}
img{display:block;max-width:100%;}
.mono{font-family:"Geist Mono","Consolas",monospace;font-weight:400;}
h1,h2,h3,p,ol,ul,figure{margin:0;padding:0;}
a{color:inherit;}
.sr-only{position:absolute;width:1px;height:1px;padding:0;margin:-1px;overflow:hidden;clip:rect(0,0,0,0);white-space:nowrap;border:0;}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------- rutverket shell */
.rutverk{max-width:1440px;margin:0 auto;background:#000;}
.rutverk > section{scroll-margin-top:48px;}

.g{display:grid;gap:1px;background:#000;}
.cell{background:var(--paper);padding:var(--cellpad);position:relative;overflow:hidden;}
.cell--pad0{padding:0;}
.cell--ink{background:var(--ink);color:var(--paper);}
.cell--black{background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);}
.cell--grey{background:var(--grey);color:var(--ink);}
.cell--mint{background:var(--mint);color:var(--black);}
.cell--rust{background:var(--rust);color:var(--paper);}
.cell--lacquer{background:var(--lacquer);color:var(--paper);}

.g12{grid-template-columns:repeat(12,1fr);}
@media (max-width:1199px){
  .g12{grid-template-columns:repeat(6,1fr);}
}
@media (max-width:767px){
  .g12{grid-template-columns:1fr;}
  .g12 > *{grid-column:1 / -1 !important;}
}

.c-2{grid-column:span 2;}
.c-3{grid-column:span 3;}
.c-4{grid-column:span 4;}
.c-5{grid-column:span 5;}
.c-6{grid-column:span 6;}
.c-7{grid-column:span 7;}
.c-8{grid-column:span 8;}
.c-12{grid-column:span 12;}
@media (max-width:1199px){
  .c-7,.c-5,.c-8,.c-4{grid-column:span 6;}
}

.headline-50{font-size:var(--headline-50);line-height:.8;letter-spacing:-.04em;font-weight:500;}
.headline-40{font-size:var(--headline-40);line-height:1;letter-spacing:-.04em;font-weight:500;}
.headline-20{font-size:var(--headline-20);line-height:1;letter-spacing:-.04em;font-weight:500;}
.h3{font-size:var(--h3);line-height:1.1;letter-spacing:-.02em;font-weight:500;}
.body{font-size:var(--body);line-height:1.3;letter-spacing:-.02em;}
.body-30{font-size:var(--body-30);line-height:1.1;letter-spacing:-.02em;}
.caption{font-size:var(--caption);letter-spacing:0;}
.tnum{font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- topline */
.topline{
  position:sticky;top:0;z-index:40;height:48px;max-width:1440px;margin:0 auto;
  display:grid;grid-template-columns:auto 1fr auto;gap:1px;background:#000;
}
.topline-cell{background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);display:flex;align-items:center;padding:0 20px;}
.topline-logo{width:auto;height:22px;}
.topline-mark{font-size:15px;letter-spacing:-.02em;font-weight:500;}
.topline-mid{background:var(--paper);}
.topline-contact{background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);font-size:14px;text-decoration:none;justify-content:flex-end;}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- hero */
/* R3: the fixed 190svh CSS-sticky stage is gone. The pin distance is now
   owned by ScrollTrigger's own pinSpacing (desktop matchMedia branch,
   RORELSE-SPEC.md §2); hero-wrap just needs to size to its content so a
   no-JS/pre-JS view still shows one full stage, not a dead 90svh gap. */
.hero-wrap{position:relative;max-width:1440px;margin:0 auto;}
.hero-stage{
  position:relative;height:calc(100svh - 48px);
  display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;grid-template-rows:1fr 1fr;
  gap:1px;background:#000;
}
@media (max-width:767px){
  /* Mobile drops the pin: no extra scroll-span, no sticky stage. The four
     cells stack in normal flow (each already min-height:60vw, so the
     stack is naturally taller than one screen) and the card flips against
     that natural scroll distance instead of a dedicated dead-space span. */
  .hero-wrap{height:auto;}
  .hero-stage{grid-template-columns:1fr;grid-template-rows:repeat(4,minmax(60vw,auto));height:auto;position:relative;top:0;}
}
.hero-cell{position:relative;overflow:hidden;}
.hero-ov{background:var(--paper);display:flex;align-items:flex-end;padding:var(--cellpad);}
.hero-oh{background:var(--grey);}

1	---
2	title: "Design fingerprint registry"
3	type: registry
4	updated: 2026-09-03
5	---
6	
7	# Design fingerprint registry
8	
9	The fingerprint gate for scroll-choreographed Persuade/Experience builds. See
10	`.agents/skills/design/references/scroll/feel-and-fingerprint.md` § The
11	fingerprint gate for the rule: **a new build must differ from EVERY existing
12	row on at least 4 of the 6 dimension columns**, checked row by row, not
13	averaged across the table. If a planned build fails the gate, change the
14	plan, not this file — rewriting a row to make a new build fit is the one
15	thing that makes this registry worthless.
16	
17	Seeded 2026-09-03 with one row per existing example site in
18	`anti-slop-design/sites/`. These sites predate scroll-craft integration and
19	were not built against the nine-device kit or the eight named grammars — the
20	Grammar, Signature move and Register columns below are an honest read of what
21	each page actually does, mapped onto scroll-craft's vocabulary after the
22	fact, not a claim that they were built to it. Where a site has no bespoke
23	interaction beyond an ordinary reveal-on-scroll, the Signature move column
24	says `none` — that is a finding, not a gap in the audit.
25	
26	| Build | Grammar | Nav treatment | Hero device | Act-sequence shape | Close pattern | Signature move | Register | World / palette | Path |
27	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
28	| Calyx | Chaptered editorial | Static (non-sticky) border-b header, 3-col grid: edition kicker · centred wordmark · two text anchors | Full-bleed botanical photo, gradient scrim, headline lead-corner bottom-left, kicker+copy trail-corner bottom-right | ~8 sections: hero > manifesto/quote > duo photo pair > index/commission ledger (`.01`–`.04`) > immersion photo break > testimonial ledger > commission CTA | Dark-inverted section, mailto set as huge italic display type with arrow; 4-col colophon footer | none — plain IntersectionObserver fade/rise reveal and ordinary image-hover scale only | Editorial print | Cardo (display) + PT Mono (kicker); cream / bone / moss / ink / rust | `anti-slop-design/sites/calyx.html` |
29	| Hōrai | Filmic one-shot | Fixed bar, transparent → dark-blurred on scroll; wordmark + "RESERVATIONS" button | Full-bleed JS-parallax photo, giant wordmark, JP kicker, two-column lede | ~7 sections: hero > the house (word-lit lede) > pinned scroll-scrubbed quote chapter > set menus (3 numbered courses) > photo spread > the room (parallax) > reservations CTA | Dark section, "book.horai.se" as huge typeset link + mailto, address, 3-col colophon | Pinned quote set-piece: kicker + gold rules + JP glyphs + blockquote scrub in/out on a bell-curve proximity-to-viewport-center function, independent per-element stagger (blur, scale, translate, tracking), `?preview=quote` hook | Cinematic dark | Cinzel + Vollkorn + Noto Serif JP; paper / walnut / lacquer / jade | `anti-slop-design/sites/horai.html` |

35	
36	## Reading this table before a new build
37	
38	Three grammar collisions already exist among these seven rows: Calyx,
39	Hyperborea and Vintergatan all read as chaptered editorial, and Vinterspelen
40	leans the same way with a gallery inflection. A new chaptered-editorial build
41	has to clear 3 more dimensions against **each** of those four rows
42	individually — nav treatment and hero device are the two that repeat across
43	them most (folio/edition-strip nav, type-in-photo or split-poster heroes), so
44	those are the columns most likely to collide again. Hōrai and Tidvatten share
45	grammar (filmic one-shot), a fixed minimal bar, a JS-parallax full-bleed
46	hero, and a bell-curve-scrub pinned set-piece as their signature move's
47	underlying mechanism — a third filmic one-shot build with a scrub-driven
48	pinned set-piece would need a genuinely different mechanism for the move, not
49	just different numbers on screen, to clear dimension 6 meaningfully even
50	though the gate counts it as free.
51	
52	`before-ai-slop.html` is not a build to avoid colliding with — it is the
53	negative reference. Any real build should differ from it on every dimension
54	by construction.
55	
56	## Alunix concept builds, rounds 1–7 (appended 2026-09-09)
57	
58	Twenty-nine rows, one per built `index.html` under `anti-slop-design/tests/alunix-*`.
59	Every column is derived from the cell's own files: the built HTML (nav markup, section
60	list, `data-sc-act` attributes, `:root` custom properties, font links), its `NOTES.md`
61	or `BRIEF.md`, and its desktop fold screenshot read as an image. Where a cell's own
62	files carry no evidence for a column, the cell says `?` rather than a guess — that is a
63	finding about the cell's documentation, not a licence to treat the dimension as free.
64	
65	Duplicates were excluded, not counted twice: `alunix-ab-r6/board/cells/*` are byte-identical
66	copies of the seven r6 runs, `alunix-ab-r7/board/cells/K1-1` and `K2-1` are byte-identical
67	copies of r6 B-K1 and B-K2 placed on r7's comparison board, and
68	`alunix-concepts-r5/reference/V3-baseline` is a byte-identical copy of `V3-chain`.
69	
70	Rounds 1–2 and 6 predate scroll-craft integration in those cells (no `data-sc-*` in the
71	markup); their act shapes are hand-rolled. Rounds 3–5 and 7 run the engine. In r6 and r7,
72	arm A is the Claude-native control (Anthropic's `frontend-design` system prompt, no skills,
73	no hooks) and arm B is this chain; `B-K1-nogate` is the r6 chain run where the gate never
74	fired, kept as its own row because it is a separate build.

109	
110	Grammar has been spent hard. Chaptered editorial now has five rows here (r1 K4, r2 R2, R3,
111	R4, r4 M2) on top of the four seed rows, filmic one-shot has four (r6 A-K1, B-K1,
112	B-K1-nogate, r7 B-K1) on top of two seed rows, and typographic poster has five (r1 K3, r2
113	R6, r6 A-K2 and B-K2, r7 B-K2). Continuous world is a five-row family (M1, V1, V2, V3,
114	V3b) that also shares nav treatment and close pattern by construction, because every r5
115	variant inherited M1's chrome and its two closing objects; those five rows clear the gate
116	against each other only on hero device, act shape and signature move, which is exactly 3
117	of the 5 non-free dimensions, the bare minimum. A sixth build in that family would have
118	nowhere left to differ.
119	
120	Two nav patterns repeat across rounds and should be treated as used up: the thin
121	scrolling top row with wordmark and contact (M1, V1, V2, V3, V3b) and the fixed minimal
122	bar with logo left and contact right that darkens or lightens per ground (r6 A-K1, B-K1,
123	B-K1-nogate, r7 B-K1). Two hero devices likewise: the full-bleed blue-hour photograph
124	with a light-serif headline in the water (four rows) and the crushed poster wordmark with
125	the example screenshots showing through or beside the letters (four rows). The r7 rows
126	record their own shared dimensions honestly — each clears the gate at exactly 4 of 6
127	against its r6 predecessor, with grammar and nav knowingly shared — so a v3 of either
128	concept cannot reuse the hero device, the act shape or the close as well.
129	
130	Ten rows carried `?` in Register when the r1–r7 block was first appended: r2 R3, R4 and
131	R5, the r3 build, r4 M1 and M2, and r5 V1, V2, V3 and V3b. Those cells' own files name
132	grammar, world and palette but never a register from the six-name vocabulary, and no
133	sibling file names it for them either. On 2026-09-09 the column was filled for all ten by
134	reading each cell's `index.html` directly (and, for the r3 build and r4 M2, its 1440 fold
135	as pixels) against `design/SKILL.md`'s register table and its "what varies with register"
136	markers: face, grain, buttons versus typeset links, ground and subject. Every one of the
137	ten reads as **modern clean** — one lineage, sans display with mono as register only, no
138	serif and no grain anywhere, one blue accent, ledgers over cards, and a precision subject
139	— which is the same read the registry already recorded for r1 K1, K2, K5, K6 and r2 R1
140	and R2. Each cell states the file it was derived from, so the derivation is auditable and
141	declared as post-hoc, exactly like the seven seed rows above.

# Design fingerprint registry

The fingerprint gate for scroll-choreographed Persuade/Experience builds. See
`.agents/skills/design/references/scroll/feel-and-fingerprint.md` § The
fingerprint gate for the rule: **a new build must differ from EVERY existing
row on at least 4 of the 6 dimension columns**, checked row by row, not
averaged across the table. If a planned build fails the gate, change the
plan, not this file — rewriting a row to make a new build fit is the one
thing that makes this registry worthless.

Seeded 2026-09-03 with one row per existing example site in
`anti-slop-design/sites/`. These sites predate scroll-craft integration and
were not built against the nine-device kit or the eight named grammars — the
Grammar, Signature move and Register columns below are an honest read of what
each page actually does, mapped onto scroll-craft's vocabulary after the
fact, not a claim that they were built to it. Where a site has no bespoke
interaction beyond an ordinary reveal-on-scroll, the Signature move column
says `none` — that is a finding, not a gap in the audit.

| Build | Grammar | Nav treatment | Hero device | Act-sequence shape | Close pattern | Signature move | Register | World / palette | Path |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Calyx | Chaptered editorial | Static (non-sticky) border-b header, 3-col grid: edition kicker · centred wordmark · two text anchors | Full-bleed botanical photo, gradient scrim, headline lead-corner bottom-left, kicker+copy trail-corner bottom-right | ~8 sections: hero > manifesto/quote > duo photo pair > index/commission ledger (`.01`–`.04`) > immersion photo break > testimonial ledger > commission CTA | Dark-inverted section, mailto set as huge italic display type with arrow; 4-col colophon footer | none — plain IntersectionObserver fade/rise reveal and ordinary image-hover scale only | Editorial print | Cardo (display) + PT Mono (kicker); cream / bone / moss / ink / rust | `anti-slop-design/sites/calyx.html` |
| Hōrai | Filmic one-shot | Fixed bar, transparent → dark-blurred on scroll; wordmark + "RESERVATIONS" button | Full-bleed JS-parallax photo, giant wordmark, JP kicker, two-column lede | ~7 sections: hero > the house (word-lit lede) > pinned scroll-scrubbed quote chapter > set menus (3 numbered courses) > photo spread > the room (parallax) > reservations CTA | Dark section, "book.horai.se" as huge typeset link + mailto, address, 3-col colophon | Pinned quote set-piece: kicker + gold rules + JP glyphs + blockquote scrub in/out on a bell-curve proximity-to-viewport-center function, independent per-element stagger (blur, scale, translate, tracking), `?preview=quote` hook | Cinematic dark | Cinzel + Vollkorn + Noto Serif JP; paper / walnut / lacquer / jade | `anti-slop-design/sites/horai.html` |

## Reading this table before a new build

Three grammar collisions already exist among these seven rows: Calyx,
Hyperborea and Vintergatan all read as chaptered editorial, and Vinterspelen
leans the same way with a gallery inflection. A new chaptered-editorial build
has to clear 3 more dimensions against **each** of those four rows
individually — nav treatment and hero device are the two that repeat across
them most (folio/edition-strip nav, type-in-photo or split-poster heroes), so
those are the columns most likely to collide again. Hōrai and Tidvatten share
grammar (filmic one-shot), a fixed minimal bar, a JS-parallax full-bleed
hero, and a bell-curve-scrub pinned set-piece as their signature move's
underlying mechanism — a third filmic one-shot build with a scrub-driven
pinned set-piece would need a genuinely different mechanism for the move, not
just different numbers on screen, to clear dimension 6 meaningfully even
though the gate counts it as free.

`before-ai-slop.html` is not a build to avoid colliding with — it is the
negative reference. Any real build should differ from it on every dimension
by construction.

## Alunix concept builds, rounds 1–7 (appended 2026-09-09)

Twenty-nine rows, one per built `index.html` under `anti-slop-design/tests/alunix-*`.
Every column is derived from the cell's own files: the built HTML (nav markup, section
list, `data-sc-act` attributes, `:root` custom properties, font links), its `NOTES.md`
or `BRIEF.md`, and its desktop fold screenshot read as an image. Where a cell's own
files carry no evidence for a column, the cell says `?` rather than a guess — that is a
finding about the cell's documentation, not a licence to treat the dimension as free.

Duplicates were excluded, not counted twice: `alunix-ab-r6/board/cells/*` are byte-identical
copies of the seven r6 runs, `alunix-ab-r7/board/cells/K1-1` and `K2-1` are byte-identical

Rounds 1–2 and 6 predate scroll-craft integration in those cells (no `data-sc-*` in the
markup); their act shapes are hand-rolled. Rounds 3–5 and 7 run the engine. In r6 and r7,
arm A is the Claude-native control (Anthropic's `frontend-design` system prompt, no skills,
no hooks) and arm B is this chain; `B-K1-nogate` is the r6 chain run where the gate never
fired, kept as its own row because it is a separate build.

### What these rows share, and what the next Alunix build has to avoid

Grammar has been spent hard. Chaptered editorial now has five rows here (r1 K4, r2 R2, R3,
R4, r4 M2) on top of the four seed rows, filmic one-shot has four (r6 A-K1, B-K1,
B-K1-nogate, r7 B-K1) on top of two seed rows, and typographic poster has five (r1 K3, r2
R6, r6 A-K2 and B-K2, r7 B-K2). Continuous world is a five-row family (M1, V1, V2, V3,
V3b) that also shares nav treatment and close pattern by construction, because every r5
variant inherited M1's chrome and its two closing objects; those five rows clear the gate
against each other only on hero device, act shape and signature move, which is exactly 3
of the 5 non-free dimensions, the bare minimum. A sixth build in that family would have
nowhere left to differ.

Two nav patterns repeat across rounds and should be treated as used up: the thin
scrolling top row with wordmark and contact (M1, V1, V2, V3, V3b) and the fixed minimal
bar with logo left and contact right that darkens or lightens per ground (r6 A-K1, B-K1,
B-K1-nogate, r7 B-K1). Two hero devices likewise: the full-bleed blue-hour photograph
with a light-serif headline in the water (four rows) and the crushed poster wordmark with
the example screenshots showing through or beside the letters (four rows). The r7 rows
record their own shared dimensions honestly — each clears the gate at exactly 4 of 6
against its r6 predecessor, with grammar and nav knowingly shared — so a v3 of either
concept cannot reuse the hero device, the act shape or the close as well.

Ten rows carried `?` in Register when the r1–r7 block was first appended: r2 R3, R4 and
R5, the r3 build, r4 M1 and M2, and r5 V1, V2, V3 and V3b. Those cells' own files name
grammar, world and palette but never a register from the six-name vocabulary, and no
sibling file names it for them either. On 2026-09-09 the column was filled for all ten by
reading each cell's `index.html` directly (and, for the r3 build and r4 M2, its 1440 fold
as pixels) against `design/SKILL.md`'s register table and its "what varies with register"
markers: face, grain, buttons versus typeset links, ground and subject. Every one of the
ten reads as **modern clean** — one lineage, sans display with mono as register only, no
serif and no grain anywhere, one blue accent, ledgers over cards, and a precision subject
— which is the same read the registry already recorded for r1 K1, K2, K5, K6 and r2 R1
and R2. Each cell states the file it was derived from, so the derivation is auditable and
declared as post-hoc, exactly like the seven seed rows above.

- Very small body copy in the dark half
- Condensed caps headlines cut mid-transition can read as broken on a slow scroll

## Signature move

A black-to-white curtain wipe that opens on photos masked as film-strip perforations.

## Motion

Intro: a white vertical bar wipes across black (curtain) and reveals the hero, ~1.2 s. Hero photos sit in perforation masks and shift on scroll. Statement paragraph fades from grey to ink per line. Photo cluster parallaxes at mixed speeds; a full-bleed red blur image scales up and the page turns dark. Condensed headlines ('BOLD WEBSITES', 'IPAD BOX OFFICE') slide in from below with SplitText; product screens rise in. Barba page transitions between routes.

Measured (`motion/probe.json`): GSAP 3.15.0; 25 ScrollTriggers; Lenis; Barba page transitions; WebGL canvas x1 (three.js); 3 video; split text; smoothed scroll (median 69 px still travelling after input stops). Floor tier: **sets the floor** (`references/scroll/showcase-floor.md`).

## Brief

A modern clean page in the chaptered editorial grammar: a cinema-ticketing product that opens on a black curtain wipe into a white hero where photos sit inside film-perforation masks, then crosses into a dark red-lit auditorium half of the page with condensed headlines sliding in. Type: Font Sans Variable, Font Mono Variable.
Ground and ink from the measured palette (#F8F8F8, #0C0C0D, #871C27). Motion carries the page through

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\Anton L\.claude\skills\lenis

# Lenis Smooth Scroll

## What Lenis is (and isn't)

Lenis is a lightweight, dependency-free smooth-scroll library that wraps the
browser's own native scroll rather than replacing it with a transform-based
fake scroll (Lenis README, Features). Because it drives native `scrollTop`
under the hood, `position: sticky`, anchor links, scroll-snap-adjacent
behavior, and accessibility keep working — it is not a full virtual-scroll
engine like older Locomotive Scroll versions. It has first-party adapters for
React and Vue, a Framer package, and a separate `lenis/snap` package for CSS
scroll-snap-style behavior (Lenis does not support native CSS scroll-snap
itself; use `lenis/snap`) (Lenis README, Limitations + Packages).

## Install

**On Anton's machine: do not install.** Lenis 1.3.26 is installed once, globally
(`%APPDATA%\npm\node_modules\lenis`). A project links it with
`python ~/.agents/skills/design/scripts/motion/link_motion.py <project>`
(`npm link gsap lenis` + semver deps + central `smooth-scroll.js`), which the design
hook runs automatically. Static HTML reaches it through an import map; see
`~/.agents/skills/design/references/scroll/toolchain.md`. The npm/CDN lines below are
upstream's instructions for other machines. Here they create a second copy.

**Version verified via npm registry: `1.3.26`.**

npm:
```bash
npm i lenis
```
```js
import Lenis from 'lenis'
import 'lenis/dist/lenis.css'
```

Plain HTML / CDN (jsdelivr URLs below verified to resolve 200 for this exact version):
```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/lenis@1.3.26/dist/lenis.css">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/lenis@1.3.26/dist/lenis.min.js"></script>
```
(The Lenis README's own CDN examples use `unpkg.com/lenis@1.3.26/...` — same version, same files; jsdelivr is an equally valid, verified alternative.)

No-code drop-in (from Lenis README, "No-code usage" — handles most common issues: nested modals, smooth anchors, scroll reset on page change):
```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/lenis@1.3.26/dist/lenis.css">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/lenis@1.3.26/dist/lenis.min.js"></script>
<script>
new Lenis({
  autoRaf: true,
  autoToggle: true,
  anchors: true,
  allowNestedScroll: true,
  naiveDimensions: true,
  stopInertiaOnNavigate: true
})
</script>
```

## Minimal setup (vanilla JS)

Two mutually exclusive patterns — pick one, never both (Lenis README, Setup):

```js
// Pattern A: let Lenis run its own RAF loop
const lenis = new Lenis({ autoRaf: true })
lenis.on('scroll', (e) => console.log(e))
```

```js
// Pattern B: drive Lenis from your own RAF loop (autoRaf defaults to false)
const lenis = new Lenis()
function raf(time) {
  lenis.raf(time)
  requestAnimationFrame(raf)
}
requestAnimationFrame(raf)
```

## Canonical GSAP ScrollTrigger wiring

This is exactly what the Lenis README's own "GSAP ScrollTrigger" setup section
shows (verified against the raw README, not memory):

```js
// 1. Create Lenis. Do NOT also set autoRaf: true — GSAP's ticker (below)
//    becomes the single RAF driver instead. Running both is a double RAF
//    loop: two loops independently call lenis.raf(), doubling scroll updates
//    per animation frame.
const lenis = new Lenis()

// 2. Tell ScrollTrigger to recompute progress/direction/callbacks every time
//    Lenis reports a scroll frame, instead of relying on a native `scroll`
//    listener (which Lenis's smoothing makes unreliable for timing).
lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update)

// 3. Make GSAP's ticker the single frame driver for Lenis. GSAP ticker time
//    is in seconds; Lenis expects milliseconds, hence * 1000.
gsap.ticker.add((time) => {
  lenis.raf(time * 1000)
})

// 4. Disable GSAP's lag-smoothing. GSAP's ticker normally compensates for
//    dropped frames by slowing playback after a stall; that fights Lenis's
//    own interpolation and can desync scroll from animation. 0 disables it.
gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0)
```

**No `ScrollTrigger.scrollerProxy()` call is needed for window-level scroll
with Lenis.** `scrollerProxy()` exists to let ScrollTrigger read/write scroll
position through custom getters/setters for scrollers that do *not* expose a
native, readable `scrollTop`/`scrollLeft` (gsap.com ScrollTrigger docs). Lenis
scrolls the real `window`/`document` via native scroll — `scrollTop` stays a
truthful, readable value the whole time — so ScrollTrigger's default reader
already works. This is confirmed by the fact that neither the Lenis README's
own GSAP recipe nor `lenis/react`'s GSAP example ever calls `scrollerProxy()`;
they only call `lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update)`. Use `scrollerProxy`
only if you scroll a *custom, non-window* container in a way that hides its
real scrollTop from the DOM (not the Lenis default).

React (from `lenis/react` package README):
```jsx
function App() {
  const lenisRef = useRef()
  useEffect(() => {
    function update(time) {
      lenisRef.current?.lenis?.raf(time * 1000)
    }
    gsap.ticker.add(update)
    return () => gsap.ticker.remove(update)
  }, [])
  return <ReactLenis root options={{ autoRaf: false }} ref={lenisRef} />
}
```

## Options (from Lenis README "Settings" table — verbatim defaults)

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allowNestedScroll` | boolean | `false` | Auto-detect nested scrollable elements and let them scroll natively (checks DOM tree every scroll event; can cost perf — prefer `prevent`/`data-lenis-prevent` if that matters) |
| `anchors` | boolean \| ScrollToOptions | `false` | Handle `<a href="#...">` clicks. `true` = default `scrollTo` options; object = custom options |
| `autoRaf` | boolean | `false` | Automatically run its own `requestAnimationFrame` loop |
| `autoResize` | boolean | `true` | Auto-resize via `ResizeObserver`; if `false`, call `.resize()` manually |
| `autoToggle` | boolean | `false` | Auto start/stop based on the wrapper's `overflow`; requires Lenis's recommended CSS and Safari >17.3 / Chrome >116 / Firefox >128 |
| `content` | HTMLElement | `document.documentElement` | Element containing the scrolled content (usually `wrapper`'s direct child) |
| `duration` | number | `1.2` | Scroll animation duration in seconds. Ignored if `lerp` is set |
| `easing` | function | `(t) => Math.min(1, 1.001 - Math.pow(2, -10 * t))` | Easing function. Ignored if `lerp` is set |
| `eventsTarget` | HTMLElement \| Window | `wrapper` | Element that listens for `wheel`/`touch` events |
| `gestureOrientation` | string | `vertical` | `vertical`, `horizontal`, or `both` |
| `infinite` | boolean | `false` | Infinite scroll; requires `syncTouch: true` on touch devices |
| `lerp` | number | `0.1` | Linear-interpolation intensity (0–1); overrides `duration`/`easing` when set |
| `naiveDimensions` | boolean | `false` | Simplified (cheaper but less accurate) dimension calc; has a perf cost when `true`, counterintuitively |
| `orientation` | string | `vertical` | `vertical` or `horizontal` |
| `overscroll` | boolean | `true` | CSS `overscroll-behavior`-equivalent containment |
| `prevent` | function | `undefined` | `(node) => boolean` — return `true` to stop smoothing for events touching that node |
| `respectReducedMotion` | boolean | `true` | Honor `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` (see Accessibility below) |
| `smoothWheel` | boolean | `true` | Smooth wheel-initiated scroll |
| `stopInertiaOnNavigate` | boolean | `false` | Stop inertia when an internal link is clicked |
| `syncTouch` | boolean | `false` | Mimic touch scroll while keeping it sync-able; can be unstable on iOS < 16 |
| `syncTouchLerp` | number | `0.075` | Lerp applied during `syncTouch` inertia |
| `touchInertiaExponent` | number | `1.7` | Strength of `syncTouch` inertia |
| `touchMultiplier` | number | `1` | Sensitivity multiplier for touch events |
| `virtualScroll` | function | `undefined` | `(e) => ...` — mutate `deltaX`/`deltaY` before consumption, or return `false` to skip smoothing for that event |
| `wheelMultiplier` | number | `1` | Sensitivity multiplier for wheel events |
| `wrapper` | HTMLElement \| Window | `window` | The scroll container |

No option above was left UNVERIFIED — every default came directly from the
fetched README table.

## Instance methods and events

Methods (Lenis README, Methods): `destroy()`, `on(id, callback)`,
`raf(time)` (ms — call every frame), `resize()`, `start()`, `stop()`, and
`scrollTo(target, options)`.

`scrollTo` target: `number` (px), `string` (CSS selector or `top`/`bottom`/
`left`/`right`/`start`/`end`), or an `HTMLElement`.
`scrollTo` options: `offset`, `lerp`, `duration`, `easing`, `immediate`
(skip animation), `lock` (block user scroll until arrival), `force`
(reach target even while `stop()`ped), `onComplete`, `userData` (forwarded
through the `scroll` event).

Events: `scroll` (fires the Lenis instance every frame), `virtual-scroll`
(fires `{ deltaX, deltaY, event }` before smoothing is applied).

Useful read-only properties: `progress` (0–1), `velocity`, `direction`
(`1` up / `-1` down), `isScrolling` (`'smooth' | 'native' | false`),
`isStopped`, `limit`, `prefersReducedMotion`.

## Integration rules

- Always pick exactly one RAF driver: `autoRaf: true`, OR your own
  `requestAnimationFrame` loop calling `lenis.raf(time)`, OR
  `gsap.ticker.add(time => lenis.raf(time * 1000))`. Never combine two —
  that is a double RAF loop and desyncs scroll from animation.
- Always call `lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update)` when using
  ScrollTrigger, so ScrollTrigger recomputes on Lenis's own frame instead of
  a native `scroll` event.
- Always call `gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0)` alongside the GSAP wiring above.
- Do not call `ScrollTrigger.scrollerProxy()` for a normal window-scrolled
  Lenis instance — it isn't needed (see canonical wiring section above) and
  adds an unnecessary indirection layer.
- Always include Lenis's CSS (`lenis.css`) — it sets `html.lenis, html.lenis
  body { height: auto }` (required so page height isn't miscalculated),
  `.lenis-stopped { overflow: clip }` (so `stop()` visually blocks scroll),
  `[data-lenis-prevent*] { overscroll-behavior: contain }`, and, critically,
  `.lenis.lenis-smooth iframe { pointer-events: none }` — this is Lenis's own
  fix for iframes swallowing wheel events during smooth scroll (verified by
  reading `packages/core/lenis.css` directly).
- Call `ScrollTrigger.refresh()` after any DOM/layout change that shifts
  trigger positions — new content, images, iframes, or web-font loads —
  since these don't trigger ScrollTrigger's automatic (200ms-debounced)
  resize-based recalculation (gsap-scrolltrigger skill + gsap.com docs).
  This applies identically whether or not Lenis is present; Lenis's README
  does not add or remove any refresh-timing requirement.
- For nested scrollable regions (modals, inner scroll panes), prefer
  `data-lenis-prevent` (cheap, targeted) over `allowNestedScroll: true`
  (auto-detects but walks the DOM tree on every scroll event — a real
  performance cost on large pages).
- Prefer `lerp` over `duration`/`easing` for the primary "feel" knob —
  setting `lerp` makes Lenis ignore `duration`/`easing` entirely.

## Pitfalls

- Iframes stop receiving wheel events under smooth scroll — this is
  actually enforced by Lenis's own CSS (`pointer-events: none` on iframes
  while `.lenis-smooth` is active), and separately, "smooth scroll will stop
  working over iframe since they don't forward wheel events" is listed as a
  known limitation (Lenis README, Limitations).
- Safari is capped to 60fps (30fps in Low Power Mode) — a hard platform
  ceiling, not a Lenis bug (Lenis README, Limitations; Lunardi 2025).
- `position: fixed` can lag on pre-M1 MacOS Safari (Lenis README,
  Limitations, citing a GitHub issue).
- `syncTouch: true` "may behave unexpectedly" on iOS < 16 — the Lunardi
  article independently advises disabling `syncTouch` unless you specifically
  need it (Lenis README, Limitations; Lunardi 2025).
- Lenis has no native CSS `scroll-snap` support — you must use the separate
  `lenis/snap` package (Lenis README, Limitations).
- Nested scroll containers need explicit configuration (`allowNestedScroll`
  or `data-lenis-prevent`) — they are not handled for free (Lenis README,
  Considerations → Nested scroll).
- Forgetting the recommended CSS, or forgetting to actually drive `raf()`
  (no RAF driver set up at all) are both listed in the README's own
  Troubleshooting section as the first things to check.

## Accessibility

Lenis's own stated position (README, "Reduced motion" section, and the
Features list):

- Native scroll semantics (keyboard scroll, find-in-page, screen-reader
  scroll) are preserved because Lenis wraps real scroll rather than
  replacing it — the Features list explicitly claims `position: sticky`,
  anchor links, and "accessibility" keep working.
- `respectReducedMotion` defaults to `true`: when the OS/browser
  `prefers-reduced-motion` is `reduce`, Lenis forces `lerp` to `1` (so
  scroll tracks input 1:1, ignoring `duration`/`easing`) and makes
  programmatic scrolls (`scrollTo`, anchor jumps) instant rather than
  eased. Lenis keeps running (for WebGL/DOM sync) rather than fully
  disabling itself. This is picked up live, no reload needed. Check
  `lenis.prefersReducedMotion` to make your own animations follow suit.
- Anchor links are **prevented by default** and only work once you opt in
  with `anchors: true` (or an options object) — an app that adds Lenis
  without this option will silently break in-page anchor navigation.
- Keyboard scrolling specifically (Page Down / arrow keys / Space) and
  find-in-page auto-scroll behavior are **not** given dedicated treatment
  in the README beyond the general "wraps native scroll" claim — no
  primary source fetched here calls out keyboard scroll or find-in-page by
  name. Treat as UNVERIFIED beyond the general accessibility claim above;
  test explicitly on a real page before relying on it.

## Verification checklist

Run these against a live page an agent can drive (e.g. via a browser tool):

1. After `new Lenis(...)` runs, `document.documentElement.classList
   .contains('lenis')` should be `true` (Lenis adds a root class; the
   `lenis-smooth` / `lenis-stopped` / `lenis-autoToggle` modifier classes
   come and go with state, confirmed by reading `lenis.css` directly).
2. No console errors after init, scroll, and `destroy()`.
3. Trigger a wheel/scroll gesture (or call `lenis.scrollTo(500)`) and
   confirm `window.scrollY` (or `lenis.animatedScroll`) actually changes —
   confirms `raf()` is being driven by something.
4. Keyboard scroll (Page Down, arrow keys on a focused scrollable area)
   moves the page — this is the one area the README doesn't explicitly
   promise, so verify it directly rather than assuming.
5. If using ScrollTrigger: record `ScrollTrigger.getAll().map(t => [t.start,
   t.end])` before and after a DOM change (e.g. an image/font load), call
   `ScrollTrigger.refresh()`, and confirm the recorded values update to
   match new layout — proves refresh timing is wired correctly.
6. Confirm only one RAF driver exists: grep the codebase for `autoRaf` and
   for `.raf(` calls — there should be exactly one call site driving
   `lenis.raf()` per Lenis instance (either `autoRaf: true`, a manual RAF
   loop, or a `gsap.ticker.add` callback — never two).
7. If `anchors` is expected to work, click a real `<a href="#section">`
   and confirm smooth arrival — this is opt-in, not default.

## References

- `references/lunardi-2025.md` — practical field notes from Edoardo
  Lunardi's 2025 article on building smooth scroll with Lenis.
- `references/scrolltrigger-interop.md` — full GSAP ScrollTrigger interop
  detail: scrollerProxy, refresh timing, pin behavior, RAF ownership,
  normalizeScroll, sticky interplay, and failure modes, each cited inline.
